summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.

summary: Many thanks to @elmbeech for the QoI extraction work in this release (#49, #50, #51). 🙏 pip install --upgrade uq_physicell ✨ Highlights ABC-SMC model selection : compare several candidate model structures in a single ABC run, from the API ( ModelSpec ) or the GUI. See the new example ex11_ABC_ModelSelection . More robust ABC calibration : a transition kernel that adapts to parameter scale, safeguards between generations, a population_size option, safe handling of failed simulations, and reliable resume after a crash. Reworked BO calibration database : stores provenance, convergence status, per-simulation seeds and model-selection results. Reproducibility : PhysiCell's random seed is now stored for every simulation, each replicate gets its own seed, and you can force a seed explicitly. PhysiCell Studio integration : Studio can now plot model-analysis databases that store raw output. Faster, leaner QoI extraction : much lower memory use, optional parallel processing ( n_jobs ), spatialdata / muspan domain inputs, and per-timestep results for mcds_ts time-series QoIs. 🧰 New tools get_sobol_convergence and plot_sobol_convergence : check whether your Sobol indices have stabilized as the sample size grows. chi2_distance : reduced chi-squared distance for calibration. qoi_func_relational_ph now works with 2D and 3D data. Database helpers: get_storage_mode , ABC detection in get_database_type , and load_output(load_data=False) for fast loading of IDs only. 🐛 Notable fixes BO: qLogExpectedImprovement was given the wrong tensor (noise variance instead of best_f ). PhysiCell was launched from the wrong working directory in some setups. migrate_to_zstd could silently drop rows. Crashes in load_output on partial databases, in ModelAnalysisContext when launched from the GUI, and in the model-selection tab. plot_global_sa_results now draws CI error bars correctly. ⚠️ Upgrade notes pcdl>=4.1.9 is now required, and cloudpickle and zstandard are new dependencies. scikit-learn is added to the utils extra. Existing model-analysis and BO databases are migrated automatically when opened or resumed, and older databases still load. The template example files have been renamed to the ex9_* convention. 📚 Docs and examples New guide to the result databases ( doc/databases.md ) and expanded calibration docs covering model selection. New ex11 (ABC model selection), a new ex10 animation, and refreshed ex5–ex9 notebooks. Test coverage expanded substantially, and coverage is now reported on Codecov. Full changelog: https://github.com/heberlr/UQ_PhysiCell/compare/v1.2.10...v1.2.11

summary: PyUnitWizard 0.29.0 This additive release expands verified quantity exchange while retaining the existing computing APIs, session policy and qrec/0.3 / bundle bytes. Tagged QuantityRecord arrays share unit/kind descriptors; homogeneous immutable append checks conversion, dtype and trailing shape (#102/#105). Zarr snapshots support verified first-axis partial reads; typed Arrow tables and complete local Parquet bindings retain explicit unit/kind handshakes (#104/#103). Case-sensitive UCUM tools validate explicit output codes and import biomedical values through actual ucumvert 0.3.2 (#125). Only independently qualified physical atoms are admitted; unchecked provider aliases are refused. Native ASDF/Astropy quantities carry an additional sealed snapshot binding; readers check named unit meaning, SI scale, dtype/shape, value seals and their own expectations (#126). Explicit QUDT/UO annotations bind a record and selected identifiers to an offline attributed catalogue for hertz, becquerel and radians/second (#127). Quantity kinds are chosen by consumers, never inferred from SI dimensions. Earlier source fixes preserve OpenMM angstrom meaning in unyt, reuse unyt registries, preserve atomic-mass names/prefixes and record actual benchmark interpreter provenance (#120–#124). All record extensions, optional dialects/storage bindings, measurement statements and attribution surfaces remain provisional . New format identifiers are explicit; old readers must not interpret them as old formats. QUDT/UO correspondences are reviewed local alignments, not upstream exactMatch claims. Limits remain explicit: immutable append copies values; Zarr selection verifies selected chunk contents; Arrow nulls are refused and Parquet reads whole files. ASDF is homogeneous/multiplicative only; affine temperatures need explicit conversion to Kelvin. Unknown vocabularies, arbitrary/nonlinear/annotated UCUM units, CF calendar coordinates, full clinical/astronomy schemas and consumer migrations are outside this checkpoint. Seals establish integrity, not producer authentication or scientific truth of an asserted kind. Baseline support remains Linux/macOS arm64, Python 3.11–3.14. Optional profiles retain their own provider/interpreter constraints, including OpenFF 0.4.0 on Python 3.12–3.14 with Pint <0.26 and UCUM's Pint >=0.25 requirement. Exact source, immutable Conda artifact, installed matrix and publication receipts are tracked in release #128 . Publication of this version does not admit the provisional contracts as stable or establish adoption in consuming repositories. summary: **GLOBES — Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States** GLOBES is a global dataset of historical wave observations from moored buoys, developed to improve the accessibility, consistency, and reuse of in situ wave measurements across observing networks. The dataset integrates **1,665 buoy records from 27 data providers across 41 countries**, representing 19,469 station-years of observations spanning 1969–2026. Records retain their native temporal resolution, ranging from 10 minutes to 3 hours, and include up to seven standardized wave parameters: significant wave height (HS), maximum wave height (HM), peak wave period (TP), zero-crossing wave period (TZ), mean wave period (TM), wave direction (DR), and directional spread (SP). GLOBES harmonizes timestamps, units, missing-value conventions, station metadata, and quality-control flags while preserving original provider information and data provenance. The archive is distributed as standardized station-based files, accompanied by provider-specific quality-control information where available. **Data organization:** This release contains 28 compressed archives representing 27 data providers. NOWPHAS observations are distributed separately at 20-minute and 2-hour temporal resolutions, resulting in 1,745 distributed time series. **Release status:** This is a preliminary data release (v0.1.0). Metadata, documentation, and data files may be refined in subsequent versions. **Data use and licensing:** GLOBES integrates observations subject to different provider-specific licensing, attribution, and usage conditions. Users must consult the USAGE metadata field of individual records and comply with the applicable original provider requirements. No single open license applies to the entire dataset. GLOBES supports research on wave climate, variability and extremes, coastal hazards, and the evaluation of numerical models, hindcasts, reanalyses, and satellite-derived wave products.

The dataset integrates **1,665 buoy records from 27 data providers across 41 countries**, representing 19,469 station-years of observations spanning 1969–2026. Records retain their native temporal resolution, ranging from 10 minutes to 3 hours, and include up to seven standardized wave parameters: significant wave height (HS), maximum wave height (HM), peak wave period (TP), zero-crossing wave period (TZ), mean wave period (TM), wave direction (DR), and directional spread (SP). GLOBES harmonizes timestamps, units, missing-value conventions, station metadata, and quality-control flags while preserving original provider information and data provenance. The archive is distributed as standardized station-based files, accompanied by provider-specific quality-control information where available. **Data organization:** This release contains 28 compressed archives representing 27 data providers. NOWPHAS observations are distributed separately at 20-minute and 2-hour temporal resolutions, resulting in 1,745 distributed time series. **Release status:** This is a preliminary data release (v0.1.0). Metadata, documentation, and data files may be refined in subsequent versions. **Data use and licensing:** GLOBES integrates observations subject to different provider-specific licensing, attribution, and usage conditions. Users must consult the USAGE metadata field of individual records and comply with the applicable original provider requirements. No single open license applies to the entire dataset. GLOBES supports research on wave climate, variability and extremes, coastal hazards, and the evaluation of numerical models, hindcasts, reanalyses, and satellite-derived wave products.

summary: IrrMapper is a Random Forest classification of Landsat imagery that maps irrigated agriculture each year at 30 m across Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. This deposit is the GeoTIFF release of version 1.2, the product served in the Google Earth Engine public data catalog as UMT/Climate/IrrMapper_RF/v1_2. One zip per state holds one cloud-optimized GeoTIFF per year (450 files; California begins in 1986), the state boundary polygon used for clipping, and grids.json describing every state's raster grid. Values: 1 irrigated, 0 not irrigated, 255 nodata. All files are in EPSG:5070 (NAD83 / Conus Albers) at 30 m on one shared pixel lattice, so all years of a state stack without resampling and neighboring states align pixel for pixel. SHA256 checksums are provided for every GeoTIFF and archive. See README.md for the format, grid definition, provenance and known limitations.

summary: Domain partitions and ECOD (Evolutionary Classification of protein Domains) classifications for AlphaFold Database models of the human proteome, plus raw DPAM domain results for five comparison proteomes ( Mus musculus , Danio rerio , Drosophila melanogaster , Caenorhabditis elegans , Pan paniscus ). This is the data set behind Schaeffer et al. (2023) PNAS 120:e2214069120 (doi:10.1073/pnas.2214069120). Version 2 (2026) keeps the version 1 domain definition files unchanged and adds the classification as served on the ECOD website (prodata.swmed.edu/ecod/index_human.php, now retired), domain structures and sequences, and the full database behind the site. Contents: 47,576 human domains (46,610 assigned to ECOD T-groups, 966 unassigned after manual inspection) from 18,037 proteins. ecod_human.domains.tsv : one row per domain, with protein annotation, residue range, classification method and full ECOD lineage (main table) ecod.af2_human.pdb.tar.gz : domain coordinates (PDB, pLDDT in the B-factor column) ecod.af2_human.fa.tar.gz and ecod.af2_human.missing_seq.fa : domain sequences ecod.af2_human.domains.txt : the domain list as distributed from the website ecod_human.tables.tar.zst and ecod_human.pgdump : the full PostgreSQL database, as per-table TSV and as a pg_dump HomSa_combined_domains , *_raw_domains , 0README : version 1 files (2022) See README.md for column definitions, provenance and known differences between files. The domain structures are derived from AlphaFold DB models (CC BY 4.0).
title: DPAM Domain Classification of Human Proteins against ECOD Reference

summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.

summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.

summary: We study intransitive probabilistic preferences through dice whose face labels may be repeated. We distinguish restricted models, in which the set of permitted labels depends on the number of sides, from the unrestricted model, which allows arbitrary integer labels. We review existence results, including the exceptional impossibility of a Chinese chain of five four-sided dice, and give an explicit construction establishing the known existence of simple cycles of three-sided dice of every length m ≥3, with no ties and a net win margin of one. We examine mixed-integer programming, simulated annealing, and lexicographic optimization of the margins. We then extend pairwise comparison to probability measures by means of bounded, measurable, antisymmetric kernels. For complete comparison data with uniform weights, we derive the Hodge decomposition of the margin matrix into an additive score component and an orthogonal, divergence-free residual. We distinguish the failure of an exact additive representation from the existence of strict preference cycles. The minimax theorem ensures that every finite family admits a mixed strategy with nonnegative expected margin against every mixture of that family. For the historical cycle with margins 4, 4, 10, we compute both the decomposition and the equilibrium mixture (2/9, 5/9, 2/9). Applications to portfolios, artistic evaluation, visual perception, and sports clarify the distinctions among independent comparisons, shared scenarios, and expected utility.
title: Chinese and Mayan Dice: Circular Chains, Explicit Constructions, and Decision Theory

summary: Mitoscope MitoScope is a scalable end-to-end workflow for long-read specific mtDNA and NUMT analysis. MitoScope integrates five key modules: 1) mtDNA selection, 2) variant calling and annotation, 3) assembly generation, 4) quality control, and 5) optional NUMT profiling. It is written using Nextflow and fully containerized using Singularity images. It can be run on either ONT or PacBio data and accepts raw sequencing data or aligned reads as input. mitoScope is currently in active development. Open an issue if you find a problem or have a suggestion. Table of Contents Installation Usage Outputs Installation Pre-requisites Nextflow Singularity Setup VERSION=0.5.0 wget https://github.com/czakarian/mitoscope/archive/refs/tags/v${VERSION}.tar.gz tar xvf v${VERSION}.tar.gz && rm v${VERSION}.tar.gz cd mitoscope-${VERSION}/ Usage nextflow run /path/to/mitoscope-${VERSION}/main.nf -params-file example_params.yaml Parameters Specifications The required -params-file argument accepts a yaml file with the following parameter specifications. See below or example_params.yaml for example. | name | description | |-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | samplesheet | Path to a headerless csv file with 1) sample ids & 2) input file paths | | input_type | Input type (options are: 'bam', 'cram', 'fastq', 'fastq.gz'). | | is_aligned | Set to true if input is aligned, otherwise set to false. | | platform | Specify 'pb' for PacBio or 'ont' for ONT. | | outdir | Path to directory to output results. | | reference | Path to reference genome. | example_params.yaml samplesheet: "samples.csv" input_type: "bam" is_aligned: true platform: "pb" outdir: "/path/to/output/dir/result" reference: "/path/to/ref/for/cram/GRCH38.fa" Optional Parameters To call non-reference NUMT candidates, add numt_profiling: true to the yaml file. This functionality is turned off by default to otherwise reduce computational load and is only available for use with aligned input. To skip methylation related NUMT filtration and methylation calling add skip_methylation: true to the yaml file. This can be used to process long-read amplicon sequencing data or other long-read data that lacks methylation calls. Sample Manifest One of the required parameters in the yaml file is the path to a sample manifest ( samplesheet ). See below or example_sample_manifest.csv for example. samples.csv sample1,/path/to/sample1.bam sample2,/path/to/sample2.bam sample3,/path/to/sample3.bam sample4,/path/to/sample4.bam Outputs Mitoscope outputs a directory for each sample with the following subdirectories. | name | description | |----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------- | | alignments/ | Bam files for retained mtDNA reads and discarded reads. | | assembly/ | Assembly output from meta-flye. | | methylation/ | Methylation calls from modkit/pb-CpG-tools. | | numts/ | Non-reference NUMT candidates. | | qc/ | QC metrics. | | variants/ | Variant calls (snv/indel, SV) | | logs/ | Log files. |

summary: Every LLM request SWAN AI-SQL (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWAN-AISQL) and the baselines issue on SemBench MOVIE/ECOMM/MMQA, the 30-query hybrid bench of the PLOP paper and the SWAN 2.0 benchmark (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWANBench), with the provider's answer, its measured latency and its cost, as a DuckDB file (gzip-compressed, 0.96 GB; 4.4 GB unpacked; 2,409,502 recorded calls) for the repository's cache proxy (serve/ai_cache_server.py). It holds SWAN AI-SQL, LOTUS 1.2.4, PLOP (the public Morrila fork, DP cost-model mode), BlendSQL 0.1.27, ThalamusDB 0.1.15 (exact mode) and Palimpzest 1.5.3 (Abacus optimizer) on every benchmark each of them runs. SWAN AI-SQL's recordings are its current ones (2026-10-23, DuckDB 2.0.0); every SWAN 2.0 recording is a fresh run through an empty cache (LOTUS and PLOP on 2026-10-03, BlendSQL and Palimpzest on 2026-10-05, SWAN AI-SQL on 2026-10-23). Always use the latest version: the concept DOI and serve/fetch_cache.sh resolve to it. Every table in the repositories replays without a provider key: run serve/fetch_cache.sh (it downloads, checks and unpacks the latest version), then the benchmark harnesses; the proxy replays each recorded answer with its recorded latency and cost. Model: gpt-5.6-luna, temperature 0, each system's default prompts (zero-shot). Replay matches requests byte for byte; an edited query, another model, or a client library that renders the request differently is a fresh request. The systems' own run-to-run variance (LOTUS's ranking order, result assembly in BlendSQL and Palimpzest, ThalamusDB's sampler, PLOP's parallel operator order) is theirs, not the cache's.
title: SWAN AI-SQL replay cache: recorded gpt-5.6-luna answers of SWAN, LOTUS, BlendSQL, Palimpzest, ThalamusDB and PLOP on SemBench, the PLOP hybrid bench and SWAN 2.0

summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.

summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.
tags: physics-informed neural networks; rainfall extremes; tail-index distortion; dam safety; radiosonde initialization; climate analytics; downscaling
title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics

summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.

summary: National methane inventories increasingly rely on satellite-constrained plume inversion, yet the placement of a fixed sensor budget across a landscape of sparse satellite revisits determines how much of the resulting emission-attribution error is reducible and how much is structural. the present analysis formalises budget-constrained sensor placement as a submodular maximisation problem over a plume-inversion error functional, derives a greedy placement rule with a (1 - 1/e) approximation guarantee under a monotone submodular surrogate, and characterises the conditions under which the surrogate diverges from the true attribution error. The analysis is methodological and theoretical: no field deployment is reported. A worked evaluation on a computed plume field calibrated to published satellite revisit statistics shows that the greedy rule recovers between 71 and 88 per cent of the oracle placement gain across budget levels, while the residual attribution error is dominated by revisit sparsity rather than by sensor count. Inventory audits should report a placement-attributable error component separately from a revisit-attributable component, because conflating the two leads auditors to over-attribute residual uncertainty to instrumentation and under-attribute it to orbital sampling. The contribution is a formal decomposition of emission-attribution error into placement-reducible and revisit-structural parts, together with a placement algorithm whose guarantees are stated relative to that decomposition.
tags: methane plume inversion; sensor placement; submodular optimisation; satellite revisit; emission attribution; inventory audit; computer science

summary: HIGH-INTEGRITY CARGO TRANSPORT AND CONTROLLED RELEASE IN MICRO/NANOROBOTICS AT THE LIMIT English Introduction This high-density research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for high-integrity microrobotic cargo transport and controlled release. Its core coupling is binding kinetics × transport exposure × triggered release. Arrival is explicitly separated from delivery: one identified cargo lineage must remain bound through transport, stay below registered shear thermal and chemical exposure limits, avoid premature leakage and cross-contamination, release inside the authorized spatial and temporal window, preserve a cargo-specific functional endpoint, and leave a closed record of residual material and carrier recovery. The central contribution is the Cargo Integrity Passport, a replayable evidence object that binds cargo and carrier identities, initial load, binding calibration, route, exposure waveforms, leakage samples, trigger fields, target masks, released mass, functional assays, contamination panels, unreleased residue, retrieval, abstentions, failures, and final disposition. Thirty physicalized derivations connect directly to 82 chapters, 410 single-page research studies, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. When unknown shear pulses, constrictions, sham triggers, second cargo lots, and carrier aging are introduced blindly, the system must lower both premature leakage and nonrelease rather than exchange one failure for the other. Missing mass, destructive triggering, target expansion, and deleted failed cargo reject the claim.

summary: Biomimetic design often risks superficial imitation and functional greenwashing. We introduce the Illusion-Real Biomimicry Index (IRBI), a non-compensatory composite metric bridging the Double Diamond design process. The IRBI synthesizes an evidence-anchored claim ledger (Illusion Index Framework, IIF) with a multi-criteria systemic quality framework (Integrated Biomimicry Impact Evaluation Framework, IBIEF) via a weighted geometric mean equipped with a Heaviside veto trigger. The methodology is evaluated across two tracks. Part A assesses three engineering artefacts (an industrial symbiosis network, a passive sharkskin foil, and an archetypal imitation) under a 10,000-draw Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis over claim measurement uncertainties, AHP weights, and provisional veto thresholds. Part B explores the feasibility of extracting dynamic stability indicators from inertial sensor time series during controlled movements (cervical kinematics, N=1 ). Part A yielded deterministic IRBI scores of 0.90, 0.62, and 0.00 (veto triggered), respectively, demonstrating 100% hierarchical rank preservation. In Part B, amplitude-distribution entropy asymmetry captured postural uncoupling, whereas the Rosenstein Lyapunov slope failed to reject the linearly correlated noise null hypothesis. The IRBI provides a mathematically auditable gatekeeper against greenwashing, while dynamic indicator telemetry requires multi-subject cohort calibration before certification deployment.
title: Biomimicry or Greenwashing? Operationalizing Authenticity via Non-Linear Dynamics

summary: The attribution of downwind rainfall changes to irrigation expansion remains contested because irrigation modifies both surface moisture and boundary-layer thermodynamics, and because satellite retrievals of convective initiation are sparse and noisy. The framework combines a potential-outcomes formulation with a honest random-forest splitting rule that permits effect modification by land-surface and atmospheric covariates. A formal result establishes that the forest estimator is consistent for the conditional average treatment effect when the propensity score is known and the retrieval error is classical, and a sensitivity bound quantifies bias under differential misclassification. The framework is then applied in a methodological evaluation using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations), where the mean temperature was 26.414 °C and the warming trend was 0.1553 °C per decade. The evaluation clarifies the conditions under which downwind rainfall attribution is credible and identifies the retrieval-error regimes in which causal-forest estimates should be preferred to regression-adjustment alternatives.

summary: Drought-index insurance for smallholders relies on weather-station telemetry that is sparse and unevenly distributed, so the index measured at a station can diverge from the losses experienced on a farm. the present analysis treats that divergence as a distribution-free calibration problem and proposes a conformal risk-controlling framework that converts station-level temperature and rainfall records into prediction sets for farm-level drought status with a user-specified bound on the probability of payout error. The framework is developed formally: a nonconformity score is defined on the joint space of station telemetry and farm-level loss indicators, a split-conformal calibration procedure is stated, and a finite-sample guarantee on the marginal payout-error rate is proved under exchangeability. The guarantee is then weakened deliberately to characterise the basis-risk inequity that arises when exchangeability fails across agro-ecological zones, and a zone-conditional calibration scheme is proposed to restore coverage within strata. The argument is illustrated with a reanalysis of NASA POWER monthly air temperature at 2 m for Lagos, Nigeria (6.52° N, 3.38° E), 2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 26.414 °C, standard deviation 0.943 °C, and a warming trend of 0.1553 °C per decade.
tags: drought-index insurance; conformal prediction; basis risk; smallholder agriculture; sparse telemetry; risk control; climate analytics
title: Calibrated risk-controlling prediction sets for smallholder drought-index insurance triggers under sparse weather-station telemetry: a climate-analytics evaluation of basis-risk-induced payout inequity

summary: Carbon-credit methodologies for mangrove restoration typically assume that credited carbon storage persists for a fixed horizon, yet staggered enrollment and unobserved baseline dynamics make permanence risk difficult to identify from satellite time series alone. The framework combines a potential-outcomes model for staggered adoption with a hidden-Markov representation of unobserved baseline loss, and derives bounds on the bias of the conventional permanence deduction. Analysis of the identification conditions shows that the standard deduction is unbiased only when baseline loss is independent of enrollment timing, an assumption that fails whenever enrollment is targeted at high-threat sites. The derived bounds imply that permanence-risk overstatement is increasing in the correlation between enrollment timing and baseline threat, and that the sign of the bias can be recovered from observable enrollment-date and land-cover-covariate patterns. The contribution is a diagnostic that credit issuers can apply to existing registries without new field data, together with a formal statement of the conditions under which the conventional deduction is defensible.
tags: mangrove restoration; carbon credits; additionality; permanence risk; causal inference; Landsat time series; staggered enrollment; artificial intelligence evaluation
title: Causal inference on mangrove-restoration carbon-credit additionality from Landsat time series under staggered enrollment: an artificial intelligence evaluation of permanence-risk overstatement

summary: Conformance vectors for agent execution evidence, and the reference verifier that judges them. This release carries 39 corpus manifests across 38 suites and 2,154 vectors in all, among them the in-toto adversarial-execution-evidence predicate, the in-toto ai-agent-action predicate, an AI generation predicate, the observed-effect predicate, SCITT COSE carriage, signed decision receipts and receipt chains, an anchor-stream verifier, ACS core, artifact binding, MCP response-phase interception, the OWASP MCP verification draft, the W3C per-check reporting format and intake, A2A agent-card canonicalization, delegation lifecycle, authority at dispatch, done contracts and receipts, grader isolation, spoofed tool output, test tampering, and ACI deployments. One binary judges every one of them, selected by the suite each corpus manifest declares. Each corpus digest is listed, recomputed from the vector files, in CORPUS-DIGESTS.txt, which the GitHub release signs and timestamps. The predicate's model is execute-and-attest rather than match-and-assert: a consumer recomputes the outcome from the bytes the statement carries, instead of trusting a verdict the producer asserted about itself. This repository is a second, independently usable implementation of that contract, so that any producer of the predicate type can self-certify and any consumer can reject a lying emitter. summary: Data, benchmarks and code accompanying the article "Two Raman peaks and transistor thresholds quantify the fixed negative charge at etched edges of monolayer MoS2". Everything needed to check or rebuild every number in the article, without re-running density functional theory, is included. first_principles/ raw PySCF output: the chalcogen-height relaxation, the five-point biaxial strain sweep with band energies at the high-symmetry points, the symmetric frozen-phonon energies for the E' mode, the relaxed-geometry z scans for the A1' mode, the cutoff, k-mesh and vacuum convergence study, and the 6x6x1 k-mesh cross-check. The soc/ subfolder adds the fully relativistic ABINIT spin-orbit cross-check (scalar and spinor runs of the same fully relativistic pseudopotentials for MoS2 and WSe2) with its reduced spin-orbit deltas. benchmarks/ every published measurement used in the article, as flat CSV with its source stated in the header: tip-enhanced Raman shifts at nanoribbon edges, disorder-activated Raman ratios and mobilities of deposited films, nanoribbon on-currents, measured mode Grüneisen parameters, A-exciton gauge factors, damage-halo widths, the Raman calibration constant, the threshold voltages of nanoribbon transistors against width (digitised) the threshold values quoted by three further device studies, and the defect densities counted by lateral force microscopy that set the reference film. results/ the machine-readable results file from which every number, table and figure in the article is generated, the generated LaTeX macro file, and the cached intermediate results of the self-consistent electrostatic inversion of the threshold data (exact_cache.json) and of the line-capacitance correction (fringe_cache.json). figures/ the figures as published. code/ the complete analysis code. summary: Companion software for Precision boundaries in spiking transport of recursive mixture uncertainty, by Chris Twombly (Independent researcher, Centennial, Colorado, USA). Version 1.2.0 retains the v1.0/v1.1 sources and replay/reporting packages. It adds the frozen S5 dependency source code, runtime-only twelve-worker amendment helper, a portable saved-evidence verifier and archive reporting tools. The numerical worker sources and original scientific lock are unchanged. The verifier passed all deposited-file hashes and recomputed all 960 candidate peaks at 90 digits on a clean extraction on the same computer; this is not full tracker regeneration or a second-machine replay. The separately source/seed/protocol-locked S5 campaign completed 480 independent new physical trajectories with paired healthy/fault sensing (960 streams, 256 scans), four arms (3,840 runs), and 960 high-precision audits. Its prespecified composite fidelity endpoint had 0/480 base failures; the exact one-sided 95% upper failure bound was 0.622167%, with exact p=0.00803329 at a 1% null failure rate. Every selection was the 40-bit floor. This supports the tested artificial population, not adaptive-width benefits, higher-width branches, calibration improvement or universal 40-bit sufficiency. Earlier 40-bit stress failures remain valid. Signed integrate-and-fire packets operate within a numerical host-recursive Gaussian-process mixture tracker. Host gains, weights, mixture assembly and forecast algebra remain numerical. Author code is MIT; retained third-party components keep their notices. The original pipeline retains frozen path/dependency assumptions and is not claimed fully relocatable; the portable verifier checks the saved S5 evidence without importing that pipeline. Original locks, analyses, stress breaches and failed endpoints are retained. The independent-machine R1 replay remains not passed (7/8). S5 is fresh synthetic confirmation, not another independent-machine replay. Cross-platform regeneration previously agreed within 5e-11 rather than bitwise; saved synthetic inputs remain the numerical reference. External-data exclusions are unchanged: no K-Radar data/derived outcomes, TartanAviation raw archives, recorded aircraft coordinates, recorded input/truth arrays or recorded forecast means are redistributed. The new S5 positions, truth and compact forecasts are wholly synthetic. Full component and internal-state traces remain local for size; original hashes are retained. Mixed-data manuscript snapshots and edit specifications are excluded. Provider data must be obtained from official sources under their terms. No neuromorphic hardware energy, latency or efficiency benefit is claimed. No external funding; no competing interests. Files remain restricted for peer review. The manuscript remains under author review; this archive is not journal submission.

summary: Firm-year panel (95 listed firms in Thailand and Singapore, 2016-2023, 760 firm-years) and R code used to produce the regression results in the article submitted to the International Journal of Financial Studies. The archive includes the analysis dataset, annual exchange rates (FRED), the Thaipat ESG100 membership list used to code the Thai ESG indicator, and an R script that reproduces the reported estimates (firm and year fixed effects with firm-clustered standard errors). A README documents all variables and sources. The files contain derived variables only (annual returns and year-end market capitalization), not raw price series.

summary: MshBench is a cross-language dataset for evaluating LLM-generated separation logic specifications with VeriFast. It contains 148 tasks across C (39), Java (60), and Rust (49). Each task provides a program with reference annotations, a specification-free input, extracted reference specifications, and task metadata. This release also includes language-specific prompts, LLM-generated specification candidates, VeriFast verification logs, bounded repair traces, result tables, and scripts used to construct and analyze the dataset. Task IDs link the benchmark files to the experimental results. The README describes the directory structure, task format, and reproduction steps.

summary: RFT-FaultBench provides training-process telemetry for anomaly detection and failure-type diagnosis in reinforcement fine-tuning. This revised dataset contains 2,630 runs (339 normal and 2,291 injected), 72,100 train-step records, and 2,617,600 training trajectories across OpenRLHF, AgentEvolver, and TRL and five task categories: arithmetic reasoning, GSM8K-style mathematical reasoning, code generation, verifiable instruction following, and tool calling. It includes 55 compound-failure runs for detection; diagnosis uses 2,236 single-failure runs. Task versions and native failure-label coverage differ across frameworks. The package includes run-level artifacts, canonical labels and seeds, five seed-grouped evaluation folds, 25 one-shot support draws, provenance and exclusion ledgers, per-file checksums, and Python example loaders and validation tools. Membership follows the frozen 2026-10-12 evaluation snapshot. It updates the earlier 779-run release; no new training was performed during packaging. GitHub companion: AIOps4LLM/RFT-FaultBench . Related manuscript: Towards Robust LLM Post-Training: Automatic Failure Diagnosis for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning. Extract RFT-FaultBench-full.tar.gz and consult its README and docs for schemas, verification evidence, and evaluation scope. The dataset continues the CC BY 4.0 license of the preceding Zenodo version.

summary: ICMarkingSynthetic is a synthetic image dataset of defective integrated circuit markings generated by physics-informed guidelines. The guidelines distinguish surface abrasion and deposition from changes to the marking itself, covering scratch, contamination, missing text, smeared text, and combined defects. Images are accompanied by labels and generation provenance. These models are cause-derived image-formation approximations, not first-principles material or optical simulations. This record contains the dataset archive and its companion generator archive. Reproduction instructions and annotation limitations are documented in the archive READMEs. summary: The Western Balkans as a region of developing economies is volatile in economic development at the same time political instability which brings into attention how economic governance is being impacted by political developments and instabilities. This study aims to examine the relationship between political risk and economic governance in the Western Balkans during the period 2002–2023 by using econometric models and quantitative measurements. The investigations focus on six Western Balkan economies. Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, utilizing annual country-level panel data from the World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators and World Development Indicators. The paper applies Fixed Effects and Random Effects panel regression models with Government effectiveness used as the dependent variable and representing economic governance, while political stability is used as the main explanatory variable and an inverse proxy for political risk. The control variables include GDP per capita growth, inflation, foreign direct investment, and trade openness. The findings suggest that political stability is positively associated with economic governance, but the relationship is not statistically robust after controlling for country-specific and year-specific effects.

summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.

summary: When a central bank raises rates, the government's interest bill rises. Whether the extra interest supports domestic demand depends on who receives it. Recent evidence finds this direct fiscal channel of monetary policy was small in the United States before 2020, because long Treasury maturities slowed the pass-through of policy rates to interest costs. We argue that this conclusion does not carry over to the post-2022 tightening. Quantitative easing replaced long-term Treasury debt with overnight interest-bearing reserves, so the consolidated public sector repriced far faster than Treasury maturities suggest, and the price-insensitive official holders that once anchored demand for Treasuries were replaced at the margin by domestic private buyers. Using published Treasury, Federal Reserve and TIC data, we decompose the rise in public-sector interest outflows between 2021 and 2024. Net interest rose by about \$530 billion, three quarters of it due to higher rates rather than more debt. Counting the Treasury and the Federal Reserve together, roughly 57 percent of the increase in public-sector interest outflows reached domestic non-federal holders directly, 27 percent reached them through the Federal Reserve's payments on reserves and reverse repos, whose counterpart was the end of its remittances to the Treasury, and 16 percent went abroad. For the Treasury securities the Federal Reserve held at the end of 2021, quantitative easing made higher rates reach non-federal holders' income roughly two to two and a half times as fast as if the bonds had stayed in private hands. Domestic investors absorbed close to 90 percent of the growth in privately held debt. We discuss what this implies for the potency of rate hikes, for the design of interest on reserves, and for reserve-currency issuers more generally.

summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

summary: Analysis code for the manuscript submitted to Kidney International Reports (KIR-S-26-00587). The study uses target trial emulation with clone-censor-weighting (CCW) to estimate the effect of early (<=24 h) vs no/late insulin initiation on AKI progression among sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) patients, stratified by a glucose-trajectory phenotype (P2 = high-sustained). Includes primary CCW analyses, a negative control outcome (NCO) sensitivity analysis, eICU-CRD 2.0 external validation (phenotypic portability), and an exploratory MIMIC-III CareVue replication. Data sources (PhysioNet credentialed): MIMIC-IV (discovery), eICU-CRD 2.0, MIMIC-III CareVue. Reported under STROBE + RECORD + TARGET.

Includes primary CCW analyses, a negative control outcome (NCO) sensitivity analysis, eICU-CRD 2.0 external validation (phenotypic portability), and an exploratory MIMIC-III CareVue replication. Data sources (PhysioNet credentialed): MIMIC-IV (discovery), eICU-CRD 2.0, MIMIC-III CareVue. Reported under STROBE + RECORD + TARGET.
title: BD2: Insulin timing and glucose-trajectory phenotypes in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury - analysis code

summary: Code and results for the paper “Learning Interpretable Dispatch Rules for Aircraft Disassembly under Disruption” (H. Saleh, submitted). The package contains: an event-driven simulator of aircraft teardown with licensed crews, zone capacity and mass balance; two disruption models, one with announced absences and one with pause-and-resume absences, both with hidden work; an independent schedule checker and the hindsight lower bound; genetic programming for priority rules; the competitors: classic priority rules, a look-ahead (rollout), and CP-SAT re-planning at every event; the result files of every experiment in the paper (15,734 schedules, all valid), with scripts that rebuild the tables and figures from them. The learned rule is priority = LST − 0.5·CERT: the latest start time minus a head start for licensed seats. Benchmark data are not included. The aircraft disassembly benchmark of Thomas and Schaus and the MSLIB instances are downloaded from their sources; the README gives the commands and pinned versions. Code: MIT license. Results and figures: CC BY 4.0.

summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. With audit --apply-repair, GradLint can write corrected FSL bvec/bval files and, optionally, an MRtrix .b table, together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs. WARN decisions additionally require --force-repair. Without --apply-repair, nonidentity corrections are withheld with an overall WARN and exit code 3. GradLint does not verify volume-to-gradient pairing. The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.7, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-23. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. Repository: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint Release: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint/releases/tag/v1.1.7 PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/gradlint/ Concept DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20847595
title: GradLint: a fast, open-source Rust tool for b-vector flip detection, gradient-scheme QC, and auto-repair in diffusion MRI

summary: Background: Vitamin D, vitamin B12 and thyroid results are often available at a first headache visit, but their relation to later acute treatment is unclear, and testing is selective. We estimated whether 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], vitamin B12, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (T4) recorded at the first headache visit were associated with acute analgesic prescribing from that day onward. Methods: Retrospective electronic health record cohort of 10,898 adults with a new headache code (G43, G44, R51) at a secondary-care neurology clinic in Türkiye, 2023–2024, with linked laboratory results. As results were carried forward, the exposure was the most recent value recorded at the first visit. The outcome was ≥2 acute analgesic prescription items. Odds ratios (OR) per standard deviation (SD) were estimated with inverse probability-of-measurement weighting, with complete-case and imputed analyses; the equivalence margin was 0.80–1.25. Results: Values were recorded for 47.7% (25(OH)D) to 77.3% (TSH). Weighted ORs per SD were 1.04 (0.95–1.14) for 25(OH)D, 1.01 (0.94–1.08) for vitamin B12, 0.96 (0.90–1.02) for TSH and 0.94 (0.88–1.01) for free T4; all 95% intervals included 1 (false discovery rate–adjusted q ≥ 0.34), and estimates were similar for a migraine index code. All four 90% intervals lay within 0.80–1.25, although equivalence was not claimed for 25(OH)D. Conclusion: In the primary weighted analysis, these markers were not associated with acute analgesic prescribing, so first-visit values may not help anticipate acute treatment needs. Recorded laboratory fields need timing and selection checks before use as exposures. Preprint, not peer reviewed. Online Resource 1 (supplementary methods and tables) is included as a separate file.
title: Vitamin D, vitamin B12 and thyroid function recorded at the first headache-coded visit and later acute analgesic prescribing: a routine-records cohort study

summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine: typed construction search, independent checks and recorded failure residues. This research candidate adds twelve exact finite-interval certificates for reflexive four-polytopes, an independent integer verifier, and a portable animated certificate explorer. Relative to the supplied Kreuzer–Skarke point-pair census, the maximum shortest descent satisfies 22 ≤ D4 ≤ 346. The prior bound 348 for arbitrary descents is unchanged. The verifier reconstructs facets, primal and polar lattice points, strict containment, interval costs, pair bounds and exceptional-census coverage. It does not reconstruct the entire classification histogram. The sharp seed constant, Hodge F2/F3-prime, GSC and the continuum Yang–Mills problem remain open. The full four-target closure benchmark has not been crossed. Graph survivors are necessary candidate configurations, not constructed semiregular objects. No new Lean formalization of the interval refinement is claimed.
title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

Those rows are present in the gut_* tables ( curated_source = infant_catalog , infant_scope = true reproduces the former infant catalog exactly: 72,468 samples) and the original deep tables ( sample_metadata_wide , sample_determinations , study_metadata_wide , cohorts , universe_studies_all , sandpiper_* , …) remain in the package for reproducibility; the paragraphs and headline numbers of that extension are kept below under Infant extension (historical description) . All other tables belong to the first curated scope , the Infant Gut Shotgun-Metagenome Catalog — the description below is that scope's. A curated, evidence-linked catalog of every public shotgun-metagenome study of the human infant gut (0–36 months) in the INSDC archives (ENA/SRA/DDBJ), with per-sample metadata recovered from archive attributes, supplementary tables and papers. summary: AIBOM-CDX-Eval: results of run eval-003 Raw outputs, scores and aggregated results of run **eval-003** of AIBOM-CDX-Eval, a benchmark of open-source AI Bill of Materials (AIBOM) generators. It measures performance (T1), reliability (T2), model discovery in source code (T3) and CycloneDX quality (T4). -  Inputs : the 100 most-downloaded Hugging Face models (10 repeats per tool) and 16 synthetic source-code targets. - Tools : aibomgen-cli, OWASP aibom-generator, ALOHA, lab700xorg-aisbom, cdxgen, HTS AiBOM, akumar-aibom, jorisbot-aibom, trusera-aibom. Each is pinned to a commit; versions are in `run_meta.json`. - Run : 6,096 jobs on 2026-10-20, framework commit `9fc720a`. Files - `eval-003-runs.zip`: the raw output, logs and `scores.json` of every job. - `eval-003-aggregated.zip`: the tables (CSV/JSON) and figures. - `eval-003_report.md`, `eval-003_summary.json`: the report and the numbers behind it. - `aibom-cdx-eval-9fc720a.zip`: the framework code at the commit used (includes the README and methodology). - `SHA256SUMS`: checksums. summary: This study established a decadal baseline (2015) for heavy metal pollution in the Western Lagos Lagoon  (Makoko and UNILAG Waterfront) using the rainbow land crab, Cardisoma armatum, as a sentinel bio monitor. Morphometric analysis revealed significantly large carapace dimensions, suggesting an advanced  age-class or high nutrient loading (eutrophication) rather than environmental stability. While raw tissue  concentrations for Lead (Pb) showed no significant spatial variance (p > 0.05), the Biota-Sediment  Accumulation Factor for Pb was above the 1.0 threshold at both stations, identifying it as the primary  toxicological threat. Conversely, Zinc (Zn) levels remained within safe BSAF limits, consistent with its role  as a regulated essential micronutrient. Biochemical markers (CAT, GST, and MDA) indicated significant  oxidative stress, particularly at the UNILAG site, suggesting a high pollution-induced metabolic burden.  Histopathological examination corroborated these findings, showing a marked reduction in reserved inclusion  cells (R-cells) across both populations, which is a clear signal of metabolic exhaustion as energy is diverted  from somatic growth to detoxification. Physical evidence of organopathy was further observed via hemocyte  plugs in the gills and tubular degradation in the hepatopancreas. These 2015 findings provide a critical  reference point for future longitudinal studies and highlight the urgent need for integrated human health risk  assessments, analysis of reproductive damage due to oxidative stress in the Lagos Lagoon ecosystem.  Keywords- Bio-indicators, BSAF, Cardisoma armatum, Oxidative Stress Biomarkers, Metabolic Exhaustion.

title: A Decadal Baseline of Heavy Metal Bioaccumulation and Oxidative Stress in Cardisoma armatum: A Sentinel Assessment of the Western Lagos Lagoon

summary: Many thanks to @elmbeech for the QoI extraction work in this release (#49, #50, #51). 🙏 pip install --upgrade uq_physicell ✨ Highlights ABC-SMC model selection : compare several candidate model structures in a single ABC run, from the API ( ModelSpec ) or the GUI. See the new example ex11_ABC_ModelSelection . More robust ABC calibration : a transition kernel that adapts to parameter scale, safeguards between generations, a population_size option, safe handling of failed simulations, and reliable resume after a crash. Reworked BO calibration database : stores provenance, convergence status, per-simulation seeds and model-selection results. Reproducibility : PhysiCell's random seed is now stored for every simulation, each replicate gets its own seed, and you can force a seed explicitly. PhysiCell Studio integration : Studio can now plot model-analysis databases that store raw output. Faster, leaner QoI extraction : much lower memory use, optional parallel processing ( n_jobs ), spatialdata / muspan domain inputs, and per-timestep results for mcds_ts time-series QoIs. 🧰 New tools get_sobol_convergence and plot_sobol_convergence : check whether your Sobol indices have stabilized as the sample size grows. chi2_distance : reduced chi-squared distance for calibration. qoi_func_relational_ph now works with 2D and 3D data. Database helpers: get_storage_mode , ABC detection in get_database_type , and load_output(load_data=False) for fast loading of IDs only. 🐛 Notable fixes BO: qLogExpectedImprovement was given the wrong tensor (noise variance instead of best_f ). PhysiCell was launched from the wrong working directory in some setups. migrate_to_zstd could silently drop rows. Crashes in load_output on partial databases, in ModelAnalysisContext when launched from the GUI, and in the model-selection tab. plot_global_sa_results now draws CI error bars correctly. ⚠️ Upgrade notes pcdl>=4.1.9 is now required, and cloudpickle and zstandard are new dependencies. scikit-learn is added to the utils extra. The template example files have been renamed to the ex9_* convention. 📚 Docs and examples New guide to the result databases ( doc/databases.md ) and expanded calibration docs covering model selection. New ex11 (ABC model selection), a new ex10 animation, and refreshed ex5–ex9 notebooks. Test coverage expanded substantially, and coverage is now reported on Codecov. Full changelog: https://github.com/heberlr/UQ_PhysiCell/compare/v1.2.10...v1.2.11

summary: PyUnitWizard 0.29.0 This additive release expands verified quantity exchange while retaining the existing computing APIs, session policy and qrec/0.3 / bundle bytes. Tagged QuantityRecord arrays share unit/kind descriptors; homogeneous immutable append checks conversion, dtype and trailing shape (#102/#105). Zarr snapshots support verified first-axis partial reads; typed Arrow tables and complete local Parquet bindings retain explicit unit/kind handshakes (#104/#103). Case-sensitive UCUM tools validate explicit output codes and import biomedical values through actual ucumvert 0.3.2 (#125). Only independently qualified physical atoms are admitted; unchecked provider aliases are refused. Native ASDF/Astropy quantities carry an additional sealed snapshot binding; readers check named unit meaning, SI scale, dtype/shape, value seals and their own expectations (#126). Explicit QUDT/UO annotations bind a record and selected identifiers to an offline attributed catalogue for hertz, becquerel and radians/second (#127). Quantity kinds are chosen by consumers, never inferred from SI dimensions. Earlier source fixes preserve OpenMM angstrom meaning in unyt, reuse unyt registries, preserve atomic-mass names/prefixes and record actual benchmark interpreter provenance (#120–#124). All record extensions, optional dialects/storage bindings, measurement statements and attribution surfaces remain provisional . New format identifiers are explicit; old readers must not interpret them as old formats. QUDT/UO correspondences are reviewed local alignments, not upstream exactMatch claims. Limits remain explicit: immutable append copies values; Zarr selection verifies selected chunk contents; Arrow nulls are refused and Parquet reads whole files. ASDF is homogeneous/multiplicative only; affine temperatures need explicit conversion to Kelvin. Unknown vocabularies, arbitrary/nonlinear/annotated UCUM units, CF calendar coordinates, full clinical/astronomy schemas and consumer migrations are outside this checkpoint. Seals establish integrity, not producer authentication or scientific truth of an asserted kind. Baseline support remains Linux/macOS arm64, Python 3.11–3.14. Optional profiles retain their own provider/interpreter constraints, including OpenFF 0.4.0 on Python 3.12–3.14 with Pint <0.26 and UCUM's Pint >=0.25 requirement. summary: **GLOBES — Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States** GLOBES is a global dataset of historical wave observations from moored buoys, developed to improve the accessibility, consistency, and reuse of in situ wave measurements across observing networks. The dataset integrates **1,665 buoy records from 27 data providers across 41 countries**, representing 19,469 station-years of observations spanning 1969–2026. Records retain their native temporal resolution, ranging from 10 minutes to 3 hours, and include up to seven standardized wave parameters: significant wave height (HS), maximum wave height (HM), peak wave period (TP), zero-crossing wave period (TZ), mean wave period (TM), wave direction (DR), and directional spread (SP). GLOBES harmonizes timestamps, units, missing-value conventions, station metadata, and quality-control flags while preserving original provider information and data provenance. The archive is distributed as standardized station-based files, accompanied by provider-specific quality-control information where available. **Data organization:** This release contains 28 compressed archives representing 27 data providers. NOWPHAS observations are distributed separately at 20-minute and 2-hour temporal resolutions, resulting in 1,745 distributed time series. **Release status:** This is a preliminary data release (v0.1.0). Metadata, documentation, and data files may be refined in subsequent versions. **Data use and licensing:** GLOBES integrates observations subject to different provider-specific licensing, attribution, and usage conditions. Users must consult the USAGE metadata field of individual records and comply with the applicable original provider requirements. No single open license applies to the entire dataset. GLOBES supports research on wave climate, variability and extremes, coastal hazards, and the evaluation of numerical models, hindcasts, reanalyses, and satellite-derived wave products.
title: GLOBES: the Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States

summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.
title: Voynich Manuscript Final Decoding Procedure

summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

summary: Mitoscope MitoScope is a scalable end-to-end workflow for long-read specific mtDNA and NUMT analysis. MitoScope integrates five key modules: 1) mtDNA selection, 2) variant calling and annotation, 3) assembly generation, 4) quality control, and 5) optional NUMT profiling. It is written using Nextflow and fully containerized using Singularity images. It can be run on either ONT or PacBio data and accepts raw sequencing data or aligned reads as input. mitoScope is currently in active development. Open an issue if you find a problem or have a suggestion. Table of Contents Installation Usage Outputs Installation Pre-requisites Nextflow Singularity Setup VERSION=0.5.0 wget https://github.com/czakarian/mitoscope/archive/refs/tags/v${VERSION}.tar.gz tar xvf v${VERSION}.tar.gz && rm v${VERSION}.tar.gz cd mitoscope-${VERSION}/ Usage nextflow run /path/to/mitoscope-${VERSION}/main.nf -params-file example_params.yaml Parameters Specifications The required -params-file argument accepts a yaml file with the following parameter specifications. See below or example_params.yaml for example. | name | description | |-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | samplesheet | Path to a headerless csv file with 1) sample ids & 2) input file paths | | input_type | Input type (options are: 'bam', 'cram', 'fastq', 'fastq.gz'). | | is_aligned | Set to true if input is aligned, otherwise set to false. | | platform | Specify 'pb' for PacBio or 'ont' for ONT. | | outdir | Path to directory to output results. | | reference | Path to reference genome. | example_params.yaml samplesheet: "samples.csv" input_type: "bam" is_aligned: true platform: "pb" outdir: "/path/to/output/dir/result" reference: "/path/to/ref/for/cram/GRCH38.fa" Optional Parameters To call non-reference NUMT candidates, add numt_profiling: true to the yaml file. This functionality is turned off by default to otherwise reduce computational load and is only available for use with aligned input. To skip methylation related NUMT filtration and methylation calling add skip_methylation: true to the yaml file. This can be used to process long-read amplicon sequencing data or other long-read data that lacks methylation calls. Sample Manifest One of the required parameters in the yaml file is the path to a sample manifest ( samplesheet ). See below or example_sample_manifest.csv for example. samples.csv sample1,/path/to/sample1.bam sample2,/path/to/sample2.bam sample3,/path/to/sample3.bam sample4,/path/to/sample4.bam Outputs Mitoscope outputs a directory for each sample with the following subdirectories. | name | description | |----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------- | | alignments/ | Bam files for retained mtDNA reads and discarded reads. | | assembly/ | Assembly output from meta-flye. | | methylation/ | Methylation calls from modkit/pb-CpG-tools. | | numts/ | Non-reference NUMT candidates. | | qc/ | QC metrics. | | variants/ | Variant calls (snv/indel, SV) | | logs/ | Log files. |
