summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.

summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

summary: Every LLM request SWAN AI-SQL (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWAN-AISQL) and the baselines issue on SemBench MOVIE/ECOMM/MMQA, the 30-query hybrid bench of the PLOP paper and the SWAN 2.0 benchmark (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWANBench), with the provider's answer, its measured latency and its cost, as a DuckDB file (gzip-compressed, 0.96 GB; 4.4 GB unpacked; 2,409,502 recorded calls) for the repository's cache proxy (serve/ai_cache_server.py). It holds SWAN AI-SQL, LOTUS 1.2.4, PLOP (the public Morrila fork, DP cost-model mode), BlendSQL 0.1.27, ThalamusDB 0.1.15 (exact mode) and Palimpzest 1.5.3 (Abacus optimizer) on every benchmark each of them runs. SWAN AI-SQL's recordings are its current ones (2026-10-23, DuckDB 2.0.0); every SWAN 2.0 recording is a fresh run through an empty cache (LOTUS and PLOP on 2026-10-03, BlendSQL and Palimpzest on 2026-10-05, SWAN AI-SQL on 2026-10-23). Always use the latest version: the concept DOI and serve/fetch_cache.sh resolve to it. Every table in the repositories replays without a provider key: run serve/fetch_cache.sh (it downloads, checks and unpacks the latest version), then the benchmark harnesses; the proxy replays each recorded answer with its recorded latency and cost. Model: gpt-5.6-luna, temperature 0, each system's default prompts (zero-shot). Replay matches requests byte for byte; an edited query, another model, or a client library that renders the request differently is a fresh request. The systems' own run-to-run variance (LOTUS's ranking order, result assembly in BlendSQL and Palimpzest, ThalamusDB's sampler, PLOP's parallel operator order) is theirs, not the cache's.
title: SWAN AI-SQL replay cache: recorded gpt-5.6-luna answers of SWAN, LOTUS, BlendSQL, Palimpzest, ThalamusDB and PLOP on SemBench, the PLOP hybrid bench and SWAN 2.0

summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.
tags: malaria early warning; causal graph learning; spatiotemporal modelling; climate analytics; intervention timing; vector-range shift; Uganda
title: Spatiotemporal causal graph learning for malaria early-warning under climate-driven vector-range shifts: a climate-analytics evaluation of intervention-timing error

summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.
tags: physics-informed neural networks; rainfall extremes; tail-index distortion; dam safety; radiosonde initialization; climate analytics; downscaling
title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics

summary: National methane inventories increasingly rely on satellite-constrained plume inversion, yet the placement of a fixed sensor budget across a landscape of sparse satellite revisits determines how much of the resulting emission-attribution error is reducible and how much is structural. the present analysis formalises budget-constrained sensor placement as a submodular maximisation problem over a plume-inversion error functional, derives a greedy placement rule with a (1 - 1/e) approximation guarantee under a monotone submodular surrogate, and characterises the conditions under which the surrogate diverges from the true attribution error. The analysis is methodological and theoretical: no field deployment is reported. A worked evaluation on a computed plume field calibrated to published satellite revisit statistics shows that the greedy rule recovers between 71 and 88 per cent of the oracle placement gain across budget levels, while the residual attribution error is dominated by revisit sparsity rather than by sensor count. Inventory audits should report a placement-attributable error component separately from a revisit-attributable component, because conflating the two leads auditors to over-attribute residual uncertainty to instrumentation and under-attribute it to orbital sampling. The contribution is a formal decomposition of emission-attribution error into placement-reducible and revisit-structural parts, together with a placement algorithm whose guarantees are stated relative to that decomposition.
tags: methane plume inversion; sensor placement; submodular optimisation; satellite revisit; emission attribution; inventory audit; computer science
title: Budget-constrained sensor placement for methane plume inversion under sparse satellite revisits: a computer-science evaluation of emission-attribution error in national inventory audits

summary: HIGH-INTEGRITY CARGO TRANSPORT AND CONTROLLED RELEASE IN MICRO/NANOROBOTICS AT THE LIMIT English Introduction This high-density research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for high-integrity microrobotic cargo transport and controlled release. Its core coupling is binding kinetics × transport exposure × triggered release. Arrival is explicitly separated from delivery: one identified cargo lineage must remain bound through transport, stay below registered shear thermal and chemical exposure limits, avoid premature leakage and cross-contamination, release inside the authorized spatial and temporal window, preserve a cargo-specific functional endpoint, and leave a closed record of residual material and carrier recovery. The central contribution is the Cargo Integrity Passport, a replayable evidence object that binds cargo and carrier identities, initial load, binding calibration, route, exposure waveforms, leakage samples, trigger fields, target masks, released mass, functional assays, contamination panels, unreleased residue, retrieval, abstentions, failures, and final disposition. Thirty physicalized derivations connect directly to 82 chapters, 410 single-page research studies, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. When unknown shear pulses, constrictions, sham triggers, second cargo lots, and carrier aging are introduced blindly, the system must lower both premature leakage and nonrelease rather than exchange one failure for the other. Missing mass, destructive triggering, target expansion, and deleted failed cargo reject the claim.

summary: Code, frozen configurations, input data, outputs and logs behind the Working sheet for MQG v0.3.8: chiral active Model H in three dimensions — computational validation addendum (MQG: magnetic quorum gravity). The archive contains the pre-registered canonical fit (v1.0), the frozen v1.1 analysis (angular torque test; joint fit with mixed noise), a reproduction on separate hardware, a second-algorithm check, and frozen acceptance tolerances for a future independent fitter. summary: Conformance vectors for agent execution evidence, and the reference verifier that judges them. This release carries 39 corpus manifests across 38 suites and 2,154 vectors in all, among them the in-toto adversarial-execution-evidence predicate, the in-toto ai-agent-action predicate, an AI generation predicate, the observed-effect predicate, SCITT COSE carriage, signed decision receipts and receipt chains, an anchor-stream verifier, ACS core, artifact binding, MCP response-phase interception, the OWASP MCP verification draft, the W3C per-check reporting format and intake, A2A agent-card canonicalization, delegation lifecycle, authority at dispatch, done contracts and receipts, grader isolation, spoofed tool output, test tampering, and ACI deployments. One binary judges every one of them, selected by the suite each corpus manifest declares. Each corpus digest is listed, recomputed from the vector files, in CORPUS-DIGESTS.txt, which the GitHub release signs and timestamps. The predicate's model is execute-and-attest rather than match-and-assert: a consumer recomputes the outcome from the bytes the statement carries, instead of trusting a verdict the producer asserted about itself. This repository is a second, independently usable implementation of that contract, so that any producer of the predicate type can self-certify and any consumer can reject a lying emitter. For the adversarial-execution-evidence corpus this deposit covers suite revision 32: 288 vectors, of which 63 accept, 223 reject and 2 are indeterminate. Its bytes are fixed by the corpus digest bf3e5befd71640757ff1b3f0af63507364b823b5e3f9059678f72f64a46e11c1 recorded in vectors/MANIFEST.json. A published revision is never mutated in place; a normative change to the predicate, or an addition to the corpus, bumps the revision and regenerates every vector byte-identically from its generators, because the vendored specification's digest is itself a corpus input. The archive is the output of git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix=agent-evidence-vectors-0.25.0/ v0.25.0 and reproduces byte for byte from the signed tag (SHA-256 ffd80cc752769d69ef13745f55cac9ab99d5a3cd5476f19359c2646597290970). The intended use is citation by a conformance requirement. A requirement that names this suite, or any other suite demonstrated to exercise the same conditions, is checkable by a party who trusts neither the producer nor the implementer. Cite this version DOI for a conformance claim; the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22758687 always resolves to the newest release.

summary: Data, benchmarks and code accompanying the article "Two Raman peaks and transistor thresholds quantify the fixed negative charge at etched edges of monolayer MoS2". Everything needed to check or rebuild every number in the article, without re-running density functional theory, is included. first_principles/ raw PySCF output: the chalcogen-height relaxation, the five-point biaxial strain sweep with band energies at the high-symmetry points, the symmetric frozen-phonon energies for the E' mode, the relaxed-geometry z scans for the A1' mode, the cutoff, k-mesh and vacuum convergence study, and the 6x6x1 k-mesh cross-check. The soc/ subfolder adds the fully relativistic ABINIT spin-orbit cross-check (scalar and spinor runs of the same fully relativistic pseudopotentials for MoS2 and WSe2) with its reduced spin-orbit deltas. benchmarks/ every published measurement used in the article, as flat CSV with its source stated in the header: tip-enhanced Raman shifts at nanoribbon edges, disorder-activated Raman ratios and mobilities of deposited films, nanoribbon on-currents, measured mode Grüneisen parameters, A-exciton gauge factors, damage-halo widths, the Raman calibration constant, the threshold voltages of nanoribbon transistors against width (digitised) the threshold values quoted by three further device studies, and the defect densities counted by lateral force microscopy that set the reference film. results/ the machine-readable results file from which every number, table and figure in the article is generated, the generated LaTeX macro file, and the cached intermediate results of the self-consistent electrostatic inversion of the threshold data (exact_cache.json) and of the line-capacitance correction (fringe_cache.json). figures/ the figures as published. code/ the complete analysis code. The development repository is at https://github.com/Tanvir-Mahmud-Mahim/Width-scaling-in-monolayer-semiconductor-nanoribbon-transistors Version 9 accompanies the first revision of the article under its revised title. It contains the same code, data, results and figures as version 8, which added the self-consistent electrostatic inversion of published nanoribbon threshold voltages, the line-capacitance correction for thick gate oxides, per-material contact resistances, the threshold-voltage data sets and the regenerated figures. Relative to version 8 only the article title and the Supporting Information figure number quoted in the README changed; every number in the article is unchanged.

Kulik October, 2025   1. The Architectural Shift: From State Catalogs to Relational Compilation A foundational problem across discrete mathematics, quantum simulation, and macromolecular physics is distinguishing between a static state catalog and an executable transformation architecture. Conventional computational models treat physical configurations as external data structures submitted to an independent processor: conformations are enumerated in an address table, transitions are assigned by ad hoc hopping matrices or stochastic Monte Carlo rules, and empirical parameters are fitted post hoc to bulk observables. While effective for descriptive curve-fitting, that paradigm divorces the representation of a state from the lawful operations that generate and invert it. Whenever a coarse observation projects away an internal degree of freedom, a state-only model mistakes an observational quotient or a scheduling collision for an absolute physical barrier. The research program consolidated in this report—spanning the native binary partner rings, the One Inverter twisted clock, the Way Between three-dimensional conformational compiler, and the tetrahedral diamond-lattice and polyethylene matter readers through §167—establishes a rigorous alternative: compilation is the continuing resolution of local relational constraints, and physical observables are typed readouts of the resulting operator algebra. Rather than postulating an external machine or assigning arbitrary binary labels to particles, the architecture begins with the minimal condition for a distinction to persist without terminal fixed points ( ) and traces the exact algebraic and geometric structures forced at each scale. This progression unfolds across four interconnected operational tiers that preserve an explicit way home at every scale by pairing a quotient difference reader with a retained frame or phase coordinate. In the first tier, the native binary ring and twisted clock establish divided left and right representative hemispheres and forward/reverse faces governed by fixed-point-free involutions. In the second tier, the planar honeycomb route compiler lifts into a three-dimensional control torus where synchronous bond torsions execute a diagonal bypass around blocked planar corners. In the third tier, three-dimensional tetrahedral chains on the diamond lattice form an unbranched two-sheeted mirror quotient across a central reflection plane. In the fourth tier, the local tetrahedral operations and reflection symmetries collapse the 72-state polyethylene rotational-isomeric-state transfer matrix into four scalar coordinates, resolving the inverse parameter problem via a rank-two observable Jacobian. Across all four tiers, the compiler operates through two governing equations that separate the underlying accumulated transformation from the perspective of a particular observer: In the first equation, local reversible increments —whether bit shifts, modular carries, planar turns, or spatial   bond torsions—accumulate relative to a held reference frame . summary: The Western Balkans as a region of developing economies is volatile in economic development at the same time political instability which brings into attention how economic governance is being impacted by political developments and instabilities. This study aims to examine the relationship between political risk and economic governance in the Western Balkans during the period 2002–2023 by using econometric models and quantitative measurements. The investigations focus on six Western Balkan economies. Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, utilizing annual country-level panel data from the World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators and World Development Indicators. The paper applies Fixed Effects and Random Effects panel regression models with Government effectiveness used as the dependent variable and representing economic governance, while political stability is used as the main explanatory variable and an inverse proxy for political risk. The control variables include GDP per capita growth, inflation, foreign direct investment, and trade openness. The findings suggest that political stability is positively associated with economic governance, but the relationship is not statistically robust after controlling for country-specific and year-specific effects.

summary: When a central bank raises rates, the government's interest bill rises. Whether the extra interest supports domestic demand depends on who receives it. Recent evidence finds this direct fiscal channel of monetary policy was small in the United States before 2020, because long Treasury maturities slowed the pass-through of policy rates to interest costs. We argue that this conclusion does not carry over to the post-2022 tightening. Quantitative easing replaced long-term Treasury debt with overnight interest-bearing reserves, so the consolidated public sector repriced far faster than Treasury maturities suggest, and the price-insensitive official holders that once anchored demand for Treasuries were replaced at the margin by domestic private buyers. Using published Treasury, Federal Reserve and TIC data, we decompose the rise in public-sector interest outflows between 2021 and 2024. Net interest rose by about \$530 billion, three quarters of it due to higher rates rather than more debt. Counting the Treasury and the Federal Reserve together, roughly 57 percent of the increase in public-sector interest outflows reached domestic non-federal holders directly, 27 percent reached them through the Federal Reserve's payments on reserves and reverse repos, whose counterpart was the end of its remittances to the Treasury, and 16 percent went abroad. For the Treasury securities the Federal Reserve held at the end of 2021, quantitative easing made higher rates reach non-federal holders' income roughly two to two and a half times as fast as if the bonds had stayed in private hands. Domestic investors absorbed close to 90 percent of the growth in privately held debt. We discuss what this implies for the potency of rate hikes, for the design of interest on reserves, and for reserve-currency issuers more generally.
title: Who Receives the Interest? Reserve Status, Holder Composition and the Fiscal Channel of Monetary Policy

summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.

summary: The onset of ferromagnetic order in one dimension reflects a competition between domain energy and entropy. For Ising chains with arbitrary translation-invariant, nonnegative, summable pair interactions, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for an ordered phase at positive temperature: the energy required to reverse an interval of N spins must be bounded below by a positive multiple of ln N for all sufficiently large N. When this energy is also bounded above by a finite multiple of ln N, we prove a quantitative magnetization gap, implying a nonzero spontaneous magnetization at the critical temperature and a discontinuous onset of order. No monotonicity, regular decay, or nearest-neighbor coupling is required. The results include sparse and irregular interactions for which r^2 J(r) is unbounded. Our results extend the magnetization jump beyond pointwise inverse-square bounds to every chain whose domain energy has logarithmic upper and lower bounds.
title: Onset of Ferromagnetic Order in Ising Chains

For Ising chains with arbitrary translation-invariant, nonnegative, summable pair interactions, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for an ordered phase at positive temperature: the energy required to reverse an interval of N spins must be bounded below by a positive multiple of ln N for all sufficiently large N. When this energy is also bounded above by a finite multiple of ln N, we prove a quantitative magnetization gap, implying a nonzero spontaneous magnetization at the critical temperature and a discontinuous onset of order. No monotonicity, regular decay, or nearest-neighbor coupling is required. The results include sparse and irregular interactions for which r^2 J(r) is unbounded. Our results extend the magnetization jump beyond pointwise inverse-square bounds to every chain whose domain energy has logarithmic upper and lower bounds.
title: Onset of Ferromagnetic Order in Ising Chains

summary: This study presents a comprehensive analysis integrating archaeological evidence with modelled radiocarbon dating, isotopic data, and organic residue analysis, offering new insights into prehistoric funerary practices in south-eastern Europe, as exemplified by burial mound number 3 at Mogila, Bulgaria. The mound contained twelve graves, including eleven inhumations and one cremation. The primary chronological classification of the inhumations was based on burial rites and body positions, assigning them to the Early Bronze Age and Middle/Late Bronze Age. Together with a shallowly deposited cremation dated to the Iron Age, three main phases of mound use were identified. Radiocarbon dating enabled the refinement of these phases allowing a detailed reconstruction of the mound’s chronological development and the identification of successive sequences of burial deposition within each period. It also allowed for the chronological attribution of two disarticulated burials. Stable carbon (δ¹³C) and nitrogen (δ¹⁵N) isotope values of the buried individuals revealed similarities within sub-phases of the Early Bronze Age and Middle/Late Bronze Age, as well as dietary differences between individuals from the two periods. In addition, a clay vessel from Middle/Late Bronze Age grave number 10 complemented the isotopic results, indicating the presence of animal lipids, most likely dairy fats.
title: The Long Life of a Burial Mound at Mogila, Bulgaria: From the Bronze Age to the Iron Age

summary: For a finite connected graph $G$, let $e(G)$ be the exponent of its Jacobian and $\Delta(G)$ its maximum degree. For each integer $b\ge1$, the simple biconnected graphs with $e(G)\le b$ form finitely many isomorphism classes if and only if $b\le7$; exactly eleven occur with $e(G)\le7$. The simple biconnected graphs with $e(G)-\Delta(G)\le3$ are $K_n$ ($n\ge3$), $C_4$, $C_5$ and $K_{2,3}$. At exponent eight, the number of vertices is unbounded among simple planar bipartite biconnected graphs of maximum degree four. For every integer $r\ge1$, there is a simple planar biconnected graph whose Jacobian is isomorphic to $(\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z)^r$, with explicit divisor generators and an orthogonal decomposition of its monodromy pairing. Every simple $3$-connected planar graph satisfies $2|V(G)|-4\le(e(G)-\Delta(G)+1)^2$ and $2|V(G)|-5\le3e(G)^2/5$. Every simple graph with a cellular torus embedding whose full inverse image in the universal cover of the torus is $3$-connected satisfies $|V(G)|\le e(G)^2$. MSC 2020: 05C25, 05C50, 05C10, 05C40, 20K01.
title: Finiteness thresholds and surface bounds for graph Jacobians

summary: Coordinating molecular, cellular, and macroscopic explanations is a core requirement of secondary biology and chemistry, yet classroom assessments still infer a student's developmental level from written answers collected after an inquiry task ends. Digital process telemetry—the timestamped record of a student's clicks, slider sweeps, pauses, and revisions inside a simulation—captures how learners navigate across scales in real time, but raw interaction counts lack a shared unit of measurement with curriculum learning progressions. This study addresses that measurement gap through a two-part validation. First, a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 86 studies (312 effect sizes; 48,920 learners) synthesized cross-scale inquiry interventions and yielded a pooled Hedges' g of 0.642, demonstrating that adaptive next-step scaffolding, paste-guarded response entry, and explicit cross-scale representations each significantly amplify learning gains. Second, using a fixed-parameter reconstruction of that empirical benchmark alongside a simulated bilingual cohort of 1,240 secondary learners and 1,000 Monte Carlo replications, we calibrated six non-intrusive behavioural trace indicators against a 12-item ordered multiple-choice progression bank on a unified Rasch partial credit logit scale. Common-scale linking error was 0.118 logits (10.9% of the critical Level 2–3 transition interval). Trace-based classifications reproduced item-based progression levels with 81.45% accuracy and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient of .768, exhibited strict measurement invariance across language tracks, gender, and prior achievement, and confirmed that genuine self-regulatory behaviours rather than interface guardrails drive diagnostic classification. Behavioural traces can thus provide calibrated, equitable coordinates for real-time formative support in secondary science classrooms.
title: From Clicks to Constructs: Event-Stream Process Mining, TreeSHAP Attribution, and Rasch Partial Credit Calibration of Behavioural Trace Indicators for Cross-Scale Science Reasoning

summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. Version 2026-10-24 changes This revision aligns the five supplementary resources with the current manuscript and adds the exact GSE163256 primary fractional-count-to-score reconstruction and fresh-score downstream verification. Earlier domain-score displays in Online Resource 2, worksheets 05 and 06, are replaced by the fixed-program paired-brain results already used in the manuscript. Superseded, undocumented competitive-null fields are removed from the current Puy13 summary display and export; the defined manufacturer-panel-matched analysis is retained. Scoring and provenance descriptions, archive entry points, fonts, table formatting and numerical display precision have also been corrected. The primary biological scores and current inferential statistics are unchanged. Earlier inputs and execution records are retained with their historical roles identified.
title: Reproducibility materials for Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity

summary: This Zenodo record accompanies the paper “Scalable Measurement-Based Quantum Simulation Patterns for Benchmarking” arXiv.2605.12502   and provides QPatLib v1.0 measurement-pattern datasets in human-readable JSONL together with a ZIP archive of OpenQASM 3.0 circuits used for validation and reproducibility.  The patterns and circuits implement Pauli string unitaries  for benchmark cases.  Cases include all possible string combinations for less than 6 qubits and strings used in Hamiltonians for certain diatomic molecules for 6 or more qubits.     Format:  Each  pattern_*.jsonl file is containins measurement patterns for all subsets for a given model/instance and subset strategy: it begins with a preamble containing model metadata, subset definitions, provenance, and (when feasible) full-pattern test results, followed by one pattern entry per subset. Each subset entry includes a required  pattern_ascii field storing the measurement pattern in the measurement-calculus/Graphix standard with signal shifting, written left-to-right in the canonical order nodes → edges → measurements (with signal dependencies) → byproduct corrections (X/Z). The circuits are included as circuit_files.zip.   Patterns in this record were validated against the corresponding circuits and checked for causal flow.   Codes for generating these patterns can be found at QPatLib repository on Github
title: QPatLib v1.0 — Measurement-based quantum simulation Pauli string unitary pattern collections

summary: This record contains the replication data and R code for the study “How much does the publication universe matter? Source discontinuities and panel selection in OpenAlex” by Vladislav Bína and Jiří Přibil. The package includes OpenAlex source-by-year counts for 2010–2025 retrieved on 10–11 October 2026, supplementary OpenAlex and Crossref aggregate counts retrieved on 23 October 2026, a provenance-limited earlier archive of annual totals, and twelve annotated illustrative record checks. It also provides eight R scripts, expected numerical results, numerical inputs to the figures, and English documentation. The default workflow reproduces the saved-data analyses offline using base R. summary: HBB2OBB converts horizontal (axis-aligned) bounding boxes (HBBs) into oriented (rotated) bounding boxes (OBBs) by using existing HBB annotations as prompts for segmentation models from the SAM (Segment Anything Model) family. It targets object detection tasks where objects appear at arbitrary orientations, such as aerial imagery, satellite data, and traffic monitoring, producing oriented boxes that tightly encapsulate non-upright objects without any re-annotation. Beyond conversion, it provides horizontal box detection, evaluation, hyperparameter optimization, an interactive annotation viewer, and annotation format-conversion tools, exposed through both a command-line interface and a Python API. 📖 Documentation: rfonod.github.io/hbb2obb , with a quick start on the bundled sample data, a guide per command, pages on how the conversion works, the confidence score, the metrics and provenance, and a CLI and API reference generated from the code. Why HBB2OBB 🎯 Accurate OBBs from HBBs : prompts SAM-family segmentation models with existing horizontal boxes to fit tight oriented boxes around non-upright objects, with no re-annotation required. 🚗 No HBBs? Detect them : the hbb2obb-detect command runs an Ultralytics detector over the images and writes the horizontal boxes the conversion consumes, confidence column included. 🧩 Model ensemble : combines masks from multiple SAM variants through majority voting for more robust, accurate results. 🛡️ Spatially constrained and safe : region-specific masking and contour refinement keep segmentation inside the object, a mask split by an occluder is fitted back together, and a fallback retains the original HBB when no valid mask is found, counted and reported rather than left to be discovered afterwards. 🔎 Confidence-scored output : every OBB receives a heuristic quality score in [0, 1] that flags silent fallbacks and low-confidence conversions, so you know which boxes to trust; the scores go in the label files or in a side-car directory that keeps them strictly standard, and the detector's own confidence can be carried through instead of, or on top of, that score. 📐 Flexible scaling : positive or negative scale factors, optionally different for the short and long sides, recover cropped object parts or tighten overly conservative annotations. 📊 Evaluate and optimize : evaluation against ground truth on IoU, orientation error, and the share of boxes above a high IoU bar, plus the hbb2obb-optimize command, a hyperparameter search over SAM inference resolution, scale factors, and morphological opening kernel, driven by a configuration file so that a whole benchmark of model ensembles is a single reproducible command. 🔬 Where the score comes from : the hbb2obb-analyze command breaks one evaluation down by the ground truth's orientation, size, frame edge, difficulty and class, and scores the conversion against emitting the horizontal prompt unchanged. 🔄 Five annotation formats : read and write YOLO, DOTA, Pascal VOC, COCO, and LabelMe, for horizontal and oriented boxes alike, with a check that proves every format encodes the same boxes. 🔍 Interactive viewer : the hbb2obb-view command pans and zooms over the annotations, in any format, coloring boxes by confidence and overlaying predictions against ground truth. Where a set ships the same boxes several ways, it names the format on screen and switches between them on a keypress. Features HBB to OBB conversion of YOLO-format annotations using SAM-based segmentation, written in absolute pixels or, with --normalize , relative to [0, 1], the convention Ultralytics reads. HBB detection : produce the horizontal boxes in the first place with any Ultralytics detector, a local file, a link, the Ultralytics catalogue, or Hugging Face, passing any other predictor argument straight through. Multiple model support : SAM, SAM2, SAM2.1, SAM3, Mobile SAM, and FastSAM families. Model ensemble via majority voting for enhanced accuracy. Confidence scoring : a per-OBB quali
title: HBB2OBB: Horizontal to Oriented Bounding Box Conversion and Evaluation Tool

summary: HIMS-CDI Synthetic Data Archive Companion to: "HIMS-CDI: A Governance Specification and Assurance Architecture for CTI-Driven Cybersecurity Risk Assessment in Healthcare" This archive contains the production synthetic-data pipeline, the prespecified correlation matrix, and the labelled 240-environment dataset used in the Phase I specification-validation study reported in Section 4 of the manuscript. The synthetic corpus comprises 240 healthcare cybersecurity environments, each characterised by 20 indicators across five groups (CTI Modality, Semantic Enrichment, Fusion Strategy, Regulatory Traceability, Explainability). The pipeline applies empirical marginal transformations (beta, categorical), generates labels via the three non-compensatory governance gates (CDI ≥ 0.70, CCR ≥ 0.80, latency < 200 ms, memory < 100 MB), injects Gaussian noise (σ = 0.13), and performs a stratified 60/20/20 split (seed 123). The test split yields exactly 48 environments (32 NOT_DEPLOY_SYNTH, 16 DEPLOY_SYNTH), matching the manuscript's specification. Random seeds: 42 = corpus generation; 123 = stratified split; 10-seed sweep = model-training runs. Provenance: The correlation matrix is a prespecified design parameter, not an empirical estimate. MITRE ATT&CK v14.1 technique frequencies and dwell-time parameters (mean 62 days, SD 28 days) are prespecified simulation assumptions, not observed healthcare incident statistics. Epistemic boundary: This archive supports Phase I specification testing only. It does not contain real healthcare incident data, and the synthetic evaluation does not establish clinical safety, operational effectiveness, real-world predictive validity, or operational deployment readiness. Phase II validation against real healthcare incident outcomes is planned (see manuscript Section 6.2–6.3).
title: HIMS-CDI Synthetic Data Archive

The synthetic corpus comprises 240 healthcare cybersecurity environments, each characterised by 20 indicators across five groups (CTI Modality, Semantic Enrichment, Fusion Strategy, Regulatory Traceability, Explainability). The pipeline applies empirical marginal transformations (beta, categorical), generates labels via the three non-compensatory governance gates (CDI ≥ 0.70, CCR ≥ 0.80, latency < 200 ms, memory < 100 MB), injects Gaussian noise (σ = 0.13), and performs a stratified 60/20/20 split (seed 123). The test split yields exactly 48 environments (32 NOT_DEPLOY_SYNTH, 16 DEPLOY_SYNTH), matching the manuscript's specification. Random seeds: 42 = corpus generation; 123 = stratified split; 10-seed sweep = model-training runs. Provenance: The correlation matrix is a prespecified design parameter, not an empirical estimate. MITRE ATT&CK v14.1 technique frequencies and dwell-time parameters (mean 62 days, SD 28 days) are prespecified simulation assumptions, not observed healthcare incident statistics. Epistemic boundary: This archive supports Phase I specification testing only. It does not contain real healthcare incident data, and the synthetic evaluation does not establish clinical safety, operational effectiveness, real-world predictive validity, or operational deployment readiness. Phase II validation against real healthcare incident outcomes is planned (see manuscript Section 6.2–6.3).

summary: BIODEGRADABLE NANOROBOT MANUFACTURING AND LIFECYCLE ENGINEERING AT THE LIMIT Biodegradable Materials x Functional Manufacturing x Degradation Kinetics This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for manufacturing biodegradable biomedical nano- and microrobots whose functional lifetime and terminal fate can be jointly qualified. Its central problem is a dual-clock constraint: the device must preserve propulsion, structure and interface function throughout a declared mission, then degrade or be retrieved within a separate terminal window without leaving unidentified or high-risk residues. The volume refuses to treat in-vitro weight loss as biological clearance. Hydrolysis, molecular-weight reduction, erosion, dissolution, fragmentation, adsorption, retrieval, magnetic-core persistence, biological transformation and safe elimination are defined as distinct measurable states. A five-compartment ledger preserves solid mass, soluble products, fragments, recovered material and unexplained residual; the last category is never presumed safe. The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Formula plates state variables, units, assumptions, identifiability, specific blind falsification tests and chapter interfaces. Research Gates specify complete-denominator protocols, analytical evidence, competing explanations, hard stops and successor forks.

summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state

summary: PRECISION NANOROBOTIC DRUG CARRIER MANUFACTURING AND QUALITY CONTROL AT THE LIMIT Drug Carriers x Precision Manufacturing x Quality Metrology This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for joint batch assurance of precision nanorobotic drug carriers. Its central rule is that attractive marginal averages do not constitute a qualified lot. Particle-size tails, manufactured and biofluid-transformed surface identity, true payload localization, release kinetics, residues and analytical visibility must be measured on representative units from the same unselected batch and adjudicated with their covariance intact. The volume treats the manufacturing process and the measurement system as two coupled sources of risk. Microfluidic mixing time, nucleation, residence-time distribution, fouling, raw-material variation and tenfold scale-up are challenged alongside detector saturation, weighting conversion, dilution artifacts, separation recovery and convenience sampling. A process is not accepted when the analytical chain cannot see the defect it is expected to exclude. The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every Gate begins with a large deep-navy bold question and continues with a blind protocol, evidence package, competing explanation, hard stop and successor fork. The central evidence object is the Carrier Quality Provenance Matrix. It binds raw-material identity, mixer geometry, delivered flows, collection time, sampling inclusion probabilities, raw analytical signals, size and interface distributions, payload mass closure, release curves, storage history and release vetoes. It preserves failed runs and abstentions rather than allowing successful aliquots to redefine the lot.

summary: Complete computational-reproduction artifact for Recovery Budgets for Persistent AI-Agent Memory: Bounding Revocation Liability. Version 2.1.0-review includes the original structural and recorded CLI studies, the prospectively frozen 120-question LongMemEval-derived study (two Claude API models, two repetitions, seven policies; 3,360 policy executions), and a separate exploratory 20-question sensitivity study (batch order, revoked-source position, three policies; 1,920 executions). Full public benchmark inputs, frozen protocols, original code, exact recorded requests and responses, usage and spending ledgers, durable SQLite traces, analyses and retention diagnostics are included. Offline reproduction uses recorded responses, disables networking for the reproduction process and requires no API credentials or model charges. Validation included 40 unit tests, the original CLI checks, 3,360 main-study and 1,920 follow-up policy replays, and reconstruction of 128 main-study plus 20 follow-up retrievals. The recorded checks found zero replay discrepancies and made zero new model calls. See verification/ for reports and platform limits. Download and extract recovery-budgets-reproducibility-final.zip, then follow README.txt. The archive contains 26,234 files; online ZIP preview may be unavailable. Correctly weighted live-and-pending quotas and reservations intentionally agree. Episodic memory remains competitive. The separate 20-question follow-up is exploratory and must not be pooled with the 120-question cohort. Scores use strict short-reference EM/F1 rather than official LongMemEval scoring. Replay is computational reproduction, not independent new model sampling. Adaptive-attack robustness, general superiority and production-scale recovery are not established. Anonymous creator attribution is used for review; third-party attribution is retained. MIT applies to original software, CC BY 4.0 to original results and documentation, and LongMemEval retains its MIT notice. Provider services and model weights are not relicensed. The unchanged archive records its preparation-time publication status; this Zenodo landing page and the accompanying release note identify the published release.

summary: NANOSENSING ACUPUNCTURE AND ACUPOINT MICROENVIRONMENT METROLOGY AT THE LIMIT STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW EPOCH / 33 x STARLI ORIGINAL CIVILIZATIONAL INTERPRETATION This English-language prospective research monograph asks whether historically nominated acupuncture points exhibit reproducible paired differences in local electrical impedance or optically inferred superficial tissue oxygenation when compared with anatomically and environmentally matched nonpoint sites. Its core three-coupling is Acupoint Microenvironments x Multimodal Metrology x Paired Control. The principal White Rainbow Epoch Hypothesis is deliberately vulnerable to refutation: analysts blinded to point identity must be able to reconstruct an independently calibrated advantage when equally hydrated measurement sites are exchanged under a concealed test condition. Skin water content, contact pressure, temperature, electrode polarization, ordinary neurovascular anatomy, skin pigmentation, photon pathlength and site-selection bias are treated as strong competing explanations, not minor caveats. The civilizational purpose follows a governing three-coupling: Continuity of Chinese Cultural Heritage x Exploration through Modern Science x Original Civilizational Interpretation of the White Rainbow Epoch. Classical acupuncture, Chinese medical philosophy, yin-yang, Five Phases and Daoist thought are welcomed as inherited cultural frameworks capable of generating questions. They are not relabelled novel SI-measurable energy fields or independently validated clinical mechanisms. summary: INTELLIGENT NANO-ACUPUNCTURE AND CLOSED-LOOP NEUROMODULATION AT THE LIMIT White Rainbow Epoch / 33 × STARLI Original Civilizational Interpretation A Research Flagship in the STARLI White Rainbow Scientific Library ENGLISH DESCRIPTION This prospective research monograph investigates a sharply bounded engineering question: can nanosensing-inspired instrument interfaces and closed-loop neural feedback produce a measurable improvement in feedback latency and electromyographic outcomes when confronted with blinded false-feedback inputs, sensor disconnection, equal-resource conventional controls and independently verified hard-stop conditions? The scientific emphasis is not a one-off demonstration or a claim of proven therapeutic efficacy. It is a technically accountable methodology in which the raw waveform, hardware timebase, stimulus exposure, causal comparator, calibration record, uncertainty budget and right to abstain remain separately inspectable. The work is organized around three couplings: nanosensing, neural feedback and bounded safety. Its larger civilizational frame is Chinese cultural inheritance × modern scientific exploration × original White Rainbow Epoch interpretation. Classical acupuncture and traditional Chinese medicine, Laozi's Daoist philosophy, yin–yang, Five-Phase thinking and the historical vocabulary of meridians or qi are welcomed as cultural and interpretive sources of research questions. They are not relabeled as verified quantum forces, established meridian conductors, or validated clinical mechanisms. The authors' new extensions are explicitly designated White Rainbow Epoch hypotheses, which may be refined, rejected or reformulated through independent experiments. Across 775 pages, the volume contains a scientific-position and provenance dossier; 30 substantive mathematical plates covering distinct routes through optimal control, physical dosimetry, contact mechanics, electromyographic inference, uncertainty propagation, causal identification, robust stability, metrology, quantum-sensor benchmarking, reliability and evidence release; 82 separately introduced chapters with 410 individually paginated scientific studies; 200 expanded Research Gates designed as falsifiable, independently executable research entrances; and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos that propose distinguishable instruments, null-test designs, conditional answers and paths for scientific metamorphosis after a failed hypothesis.

summary: This conceptual theory-building paper develops an interdisciplinary framework for understanding cancer as a model-admissible, potentially persistent system state emerging within complex adaptive biological systems. Building upon evolutionary oncology, dynamical systems theory, cancer-attractor research, tumor plasticity, and adaptive therapy, the study examines how malignant cellular populations may achieve conditional persistence through feedback, selection, environmental constraints, and adaptive reorganization. The central proposition distinguishes biological possibility, dynamical stability, and clinical desirability. Cancer is not described as beneficial or universally stable, but as a pathological configuration whose emergence and persistence may be investigated through formal systems models. The paper integrates three author-developed research architectures: the Akarkach Seven-Stage Emergence Model (A7SEM), A7SEM Reverse, and Pre-Inference Governance Architecture (PIGA). A7SEM provides seven interacting analytical dimensions for studying emergent configurations across biological systems. A7SEM Reverse examines counterhypotheses, contradictory evidence, dependency structures, and falsifiability. PIGA separates the admission of scientific inferences from authorization for consequential actions. Four testable research hypotheses, competing explanations, mathematical templates, and falsification criteria are presented. The framework is further connected to artificial intelligence through structural comparisons involving emergence, uncertainty, observability, and system governance. The study extends the theoretical foundations of the monograph Cancer as a Legitimate System State and connects related publications within the Faith Poetry Research Series. Its principal contribution is an integrated evolutionary, systems-theoretical, and epistemic framework for investigating malignant persistence without conflating mathematical coherence with empirical confirmation or clinical validity. This publication presents theoretical research and a proposed empirical research agenda. It does not establish a validated clinical prediction model, diagnostic procedure, or cancer treatment.

title: Cancer as a Legitimate System State: Attractor Dynamics, Evolutionary Plasticity, and Epistemic Governance in Oncology

summary: Here I show my solution to the Hodge Conjecture using my framework and ansatz formulation. The paper starts in 1D, from a simple sieve in mod 9 to a continuum projection, then from a 2D variety in mod 9k, to a continuum projection in 2D which can be map to any elliptic curve with Hasse-Weil operator, doing it back and forward with the inverse operator, linking elliptic curves with continuum topologies or fluid fields, and discovering that the Hasse-Weil function can be the filter we need to detect anomalies, this can allow us to extend this framework to higher dimensions with the master ansatz in 3D.
title: Discrete-Continuum Topology and the Hodge Conjecture: A Compressible Maxwell-Navier-Stokes and Modulo-9 Sieve Framework

summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): trends.polyhelper.ai/markets , trends.polyhelper.ai/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

summary: Spatial Methods Workbench is a citation-aware R Shiny environment with 12 guided workflows for spatial autocorrelation, conditional networks, spatially adjusted 2D and 3D networks, spatially varying networks, prediction, clustering, image-regression screening, mediation, and statistical shape analysis. Version 0.4.0 re-targets the three advanced network paths to the current public engines. The ISPat 2D and ISPat 3D paths call the CRAN package ISPAT3D 0.3.1 ( ispat3d_fit_2d for the section-wise planar fit and ispat3d_fit for the pooled volumetric fit: Matern-3/2 Vecchia Gaussian-process adjustment on spatially balanced anchors followed by a shared-plus-zone factor covariance fitted by Gaussian maximum likelihood, reported as signed zone partial correlations). The GP-GHS path calls GPGHS 1.0.1 ( gpghs_graph ) with the shrinkage-factor selection rule and AND symmetry of the accompanying article, and returns the GPGHS edge table with scores and signs. The retired ISPAT 0.1.0, ISPAT3D 0.1.1, and GPGHS 0.1.0 interfaces targeted by v0.3.1 no longer exist upstream. New controls expose factor rank, anchor budget, Vecchia neighbors, optimizer iterations, section handling, threads, and seeds; readiness checks require at least two zones with more rows than markers; result manifests record the engine package, version, and function; and real adapter smoke tests run whenever the engines are installed. This complete source distribution contains the installable Workbench package, Shiny application, five executable vignettes, compact simulated datasets, complete documentation, automated checks, and locally bundled package sources for the exact CRAN ISPAT3D 0.3.1 and GPGHS 1.0.1 engines. install-complete.R installs those local engine copies and the single compiled dependency gpboost without cloning their repositories. A curated public-source bundle also preserves license-safe regression, clustering, neural, SV-NN, STCAR, and SBLF source connected to the Workbench adaptations and related-method provenance. Exact engine calls, built-in adaptations, and related screening workflows remain explicitly distinguished. Large curriculum translations, media, Git history, and platform-specific compiled objects are omitted because they do not execute a Workbench analysis. Installation Download and extract the release, then run Rscript install-complete.R , Rscript verify-installation.R , and Rscript tests/testthat.R . The README contains platform prerequisites, engine options, verification, local launch, Docker, privacy, and troubleshooting guidance. Missing CRAN dependencies may be downloaded; the two direct method repositories do not need to be downloaded separately. The complete bibliography is included in REFERENCES.md and in result bundles. Public sources are identified by repository, commit, version, license, retained scope, and role in vendor/manifest.json . summary: TripLibre is an open-source, local-first iOS application designed for personal mobility tracking and travel behavior research. It records location data in the background, reconstructs daily travel activities into visits, trips, transportation modes, and trip chains. It allows users to review and correct inferred travel records. The application supports exporting structured mobility datasets in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and SQLite formats, with a Python loader for further analysis. By combining automated GPS-based travel detection with user-controlled data management, TripLibre aims to lower the technical and financial barriers to collecting travel behavior data. Its broader vision is to provide researchers, educational institutions, and resource-constrained communities with an accessible and adaptable alternative to proprietary travel survey technologies, while preserving individual control over sensitive location information. Documentation: https://hhtdiary.org/triplibre/docs/

summary: RASHER begins as a fork of BACoN 0.4.0 (commit 4fdec16, which includes the samtools consensus -C 20 change below), adapted to Illumina short reads. Everything under "BACoN changelog" is the parent tool's history, kept for provenance. Changed Renamed throughout: the package, command, log ( rasher.log ) and lock file ( .rasher.lock ) are rasher . The pipeline reads Illumina short reads , paired or single-end. sample_R1 / sample_R2 , sample_1 / _2 sample.R1 / .R2 and sample.1 / .2 files (bcl2fastq _001 tails included) pair into one sample, in flat folders, subfolders and sample sheets; a file without a mate is a single-end sample, and unmated files next to a sample's pairs are skipped with a warning. A pair is baited whole when either mate matches the reference, mates travel together through every step ( 1_extracted/<sample>_R1/_R2 , 2_filtered/... ), and a desynchronised pair is an error, whether the mates carry identical names or /1 /2 suffixes. Baiting aligns with minimap2 -x sr (BBDuk baits pairs natively with in2= / outm2= ). --keep-bam now keeps the baited reads aligned to the reference (paired samples: a proper paired BAM). Filtering: fastp (adapter trimming, quality and length filters; its JSON and HTML reports land in logs/2_filter/ where MultiQC finds them) followed by deterministic, evenly spread subsampling of the reads (pairs kept whole) to --target-depth . Filtlong, --keep-percent and --filter-by-reference are gone; --min-read-length defaults to 50. Fasta reads skip fastp and are filtered by length. Templated assembly aligns pairs with minimap2 -ax sr and calls samtools consensus -X hiseq (call quality at least 20, as BACoN's unreleased change at the time of the fork). De novo assembly: SKESA ( -a skesa ; the recommended de novo assembler — on the real-data benchmark its SNP distances matched SPAdes' with far fewer contigs) or SPAdes ( -a spades , --isolate ; writes the assembly graph, more robust below ~30x depth). Flye and myloasm are gone, with --read-type and --min-size . --snp-method auto is minimap2 for templated assemblies and SKA2 for SPAdes and SKESA assemblies. -m/--memory also sizes SPAdes and SKESA (it was BBDuk-only). A paired sample X next to a sample named X_R1 or X_R2 is an error (their outputs would collide). No assembler flags circular contigs any more, so SKA2's circular-contig end extension no longer applies. Single-end extraction matches read names with a trailing /1 or /2 stripped, as aligners report them. Output folders of BACoN do not resume under RASHER (the checkpoint fingerprints are seeded with the tool's name; every step runs again); BACoN VCFs are rewritten. Checkpoints record each step's own output signature, and a result is only reused when its output is still the file it wrote: a sample returning to a sheet can no longer pick up reads another sample wrote over. Switching a sample between single-end and paired (or fasta and fastq) removes the other shape's files. BBDuk's paired outputs are checked mate against mate, like minimap2's (a desynchronised pair fails the sample); mates named .1 / .2 ( fastq-dump --readids ) pair; the unpaired-reads file of fasterq-dump --split-3 next to its pair is skipped with a warning; a file cannot pair with a link to itself, and files that look like mates but do not pair are warned about. Stale fastp reports are removed on rerun and for samples that fail at baiting. The report and MultiQC drop the circular-contigs column (no short-read assembler flags circles) and say that read pairs were kept whole when either mate matched.
title: RASHER: Bait, Assemble and Compare Illumina short reads

summary: Entity Matching identifies records that refer to the same real-world entity across one or more data sources. It is a key step in data integration and data cleaning. In practice, real-world datasets are often incomplete, and missing attribute values can significantly reduce the accuracy of traditional and learning-based methods. This presentation introduces a technique that uses Sentence Transformers to address EM under incomplete data. Records are represented as dense semantic embeddings, which allows the approach to capture contextual similarity between tuples even when some attribute values are missing. These embeddings support both the recovery of missing information and the matching of records. Experiments on benchmark datasets with varying levels of missingness show that the approach improves the robustness of entity matching on incomplete data.
title: A Sentence Transformer Based Technique for Entity Matching within Incomplete Data

summary: This record contains the scenario bank, raw transcripts and supporting files for the study " A Faith-Aware Ethical Violation Taxonomy for LLMs in Mental Health Counseling with an Islamic Case Study " (submitted to JMIR Mental Health). Resize keeps keypoints as floats aligned with the image (they were truncated to integers); Rotate90 maps keypoints exactly (they were 1 px off on even image sizes). Resize(keep_ar=True) gives the correct shape (width and height were swapped). GridMask drops the intended part of the image, about (1 - ratio)² (it dropped ~94%). "reverse" is the inverse mode; "reserve" still works. Stream(ignore_fast_mode=...) always overrides its transforms, including nested streams. Unknown modes of Blur , CvtColor and GridMask are rejected when the transform is created. Stream(shuffle=True) now actually shuffles the transforms. New Distance maps ( 'D' , dict key distancnce fields: float16 / float32 / float64 , HxW or HxWxC . Bilinear interpolation, values rescaled by scaling transforms, and no false boundaries from zero padding. solt.utils.mask_to_sdf` computes sisks. Bounding boxes ( 'B' , dict key bboxes ): solt.BoundingBoxes accepts and exports VOC, COCO, YOLO and cxcywh, with a label per box. Boxes are clipped to thorm; Stream drops the ones mostly outside ofthe image or much smaller relative to it, together with their labels. to_torch gives the torchvision detection target. (#42) Stream(in_place=True) : transforms do not copy data unless necessary; in_place=False copies the input once. Crop corner modes 'lt' , 'rt' , 'lb' ,entation (#97). Random cutout sizes in CutOut (#37). Brightness(relative=True) : brightness chaintensity (#60). BrightnessContrast : brightness and contrast in one step (#43). Keypoints in RandomResizedCrop ; tuple n Fixes DataContainer no longer modifies the giveansforms without data_indices apply to allitems of every call. RandomResizedCrop resizes masks, accepts , and no longer produces empty crops of thinimages. optimize_stack=True no longer loses trans, no longer changes the transforms of thestream, keeps the perspective of a fused Projection , and works with Rotate90 . Projection keeps the warped image inside e cut off). from_dict no longer modifies the given configuration, and rejects malformed ones. CvtColor raises a clear error for unsuppoorch accepts HxW grayscale images; DTYPES_MAX for uint16` is 65535. summary: TripLibre is an open-source, local-first iOS application designed for personal mobility tracking and travel behavior research. It records location data in the background, reconstructs daily travel activities into visits, trips, transportation modes, and trip chains. It allows users to review and correct inferred travel records. The application supports exporting structured mobility datasets in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and SQLite formats, with a Python loader for further analysis. By combining automated GPS-based travel detection with user-controlled data management, TripLibre aims to lower the technical and financial barriers to collecting travel behavior data. Its broader vision is to provide researchers, educational institutions, and resource-constrained communities with an accessible and adaptable alternative to proprietary travel survey technologies, while preserving individual control over sensitive location information. Documentation: https://hhtdiary.org/triplibre/docs/
title: TripLibre: An Open-Source, Privacy-First Travel Diary for Mobility Research

summary: Background/Objectives : With the advent of the current digital health age, opportunities for interacting with health systems have grown not only more frequent but also variable in type, spanning across emergent care settings, routine outpatient follow-up, as well as at-home telemedicine-based platforms. In light of initiatives to re-design electronic medical records (EMR) to more meaningfully curate evidence-based insights, our research objective is focused on harnessing underutilized data features (i.e., time-ordered events) to map the complex interactions that patients undergo within their health systems. We posit that inclusion of information associated with sequential patterns will help more accurately simulate care pathways and outcomes. We report preliminary data on care utilization patterns among cohorts of patients diagnosed with chronic disease. Methods : De-identified data were extracted from the MedStar Health AIM-AHEAD Data Bridge (AADB)’s Chronic Disease repository. EMRs were queried for patients with confirmed diagnoses for diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E10.X or E11.X) as well as heart failure (ICD-10: I50.X). That figure is drawn by the authors rather than produced by the pipeline, so the value had not followed the recomputation. The version also updates the expected wordings in scripts/15_audit_manuscript_numbers.py so that the audit tracks the current manuscript text; run against the revised manuscript it reconciles all 460 numerical claims with the archived result files. That audit located one error in the manuscript, which this version documents rather than changes: the last row of Table 7 carried the standard error of the pooled bootstrap, 0.236, where the stratified procedure gives 0.169. No data, code path or result changed; every result table is identical to v1.0.3.   Version 1.0.3 (2026-10-24) responds to the second editorial assessment of the third review round. The bootstrap of the support-restricted subsample is now stratified by adoption cohort with 2,000 replications, replacing pooled resampling of the 34 treated countries with 499: one cohort retains a single treated country and was absent from 191 of the 499 pooled replications, so the aggregation ran over five cohorts instead of six and the estimand changed inside the bootstrap. Equivalence within a quarter of an ordinal step consequently holds for five of the eight outcomes instead of four, and the ratio of restricted to full-sample standard errors becomes 1.44-2.67 (median 2.48) instead of 1.73-3.63 (median 2.44).
