summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.
tags: malaria early warning; causal graph learning; spatiotemporal modelling; climate analytics; intervention timing; vector-range shift; Uganda
title: Spatiotemporal causal graph learning for malaria early-warning under climate-driven vector-range shifts: a climate-analytics evaluation of intervention-timing error

summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.
tags: physics-informed neural networks; rainfall extremes; tail-index distortion; dam safety; radiosonde initialization; climate analytics; downscaling
title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics

summary: HIGH-INTEGRITY CARGO TRANSPORT AND CONTROLLED RELEASE IN MICRO/NANOROBOTICS AT THE LIMIT English Introduction This high-density research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for high-integrity microrobotic cargo transport and controlled release. Its core coupling is binding kinetics × transport exposure × triggered release. Arrival is explicitly separated from delivery: one identified cargo lineage must remain bound through transport, stay below registered shear thermal and chemical exposure limits, avoid premature leakage and cross-contamination, release inside the authorized spatial and temporal window, preserve a cargo-specific functional endpoint, and leave a closed record of residual material and carrier recovery. The central contribution is the Cargo Integrity Passport, a replayable evidence object that binds cargo and carrier identities, initial load, binding calibration, route, exposure waveforms, leakage samples, trigger fields, target masks, released mass, functional assays, contamination panels, unreleased residue, retrieval, abstentions, failures, and final disposition. Thirty physicalized derivations connect directly to 82 chapters, 410 single-page research studies, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. When unknown shear pulses, constrictions, sham triggers, second cargo lots, and carrier aging are introduced blindly, the system must lower both premature leakage and nonrelease rather than exchange one failure for the other. Missing mass, destructive triggering, target expansion, and deleted failed cargo reject the claim.

summary: Biomimetic design often risks superficial imitation and functional greenwashing. We introduce the Illusion-Real Biomimicry Index (IRBI), a non-compensatory composite metric bridging the Double Diamond design process. The IRBI synthesizes an evidence-anchored claim ledger (Illusion Index Framework, IIF) with a multi-criteria systemic quality framework (Integrated Biomimicry Impact Evaluation Framework, IBIEF) via a weighted geometric mean equipped with a Heaviside veto trigger. The methodology is evaluated across two tracks. Part A assesses three engineering artefacts (an industrial symbiosis network, a passive sharkskin foil, and an archetypal imitation) under a 10,000-draw Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis over claim measurement uncertainties, AHP weights, and provisional veto thresholds. Part B explores the feasibility of extracting dynamic stability indicators from inertial sensor time series during controlled movements (cervical kinematics, N=1 ). Part A yielded deterministic IRBI scores of 0.90, 0.62, and 0.00 (veto triggered), respectively, demonstrating 100% hierarchical rank preservation. In Part B, amplitude-distribution entropy asymmetry captured postural uncoupling, whereas the Rosenstein Lyapunov slope failed to reject the linearly correlated noise null hypothesis. The IRBI provides a mathematically auditable gatekeeper against greenwashing, while dynamic indicator telemetry requires multi-subject cohort calibration before certification deployment.
title: Biomimicry or Greenwashing? Operationalizing Authenticity via Non-Linear Dynamics

summary: Drought-index insurance for smallholders relies on weather-station telemetry that is sparse and unevenly distributed, so the index measured at a station can diverge from the losses experienced on a farm. the present analysis treats that divergence as a distribution-free calibration problem and proposes a conformal risk-controlling framework that converts station-level temperature and rainfall records into prediction sets for farm-level drought status with a user-specified bound on the probability of payout error. The framework is developed formally: a nonconformity score is defined on the joint space of station telemetry and farm-level loss indicators, a split-conformal calibration procedure is stated, and a finite-sample guarantee on the marginal payout-error rate is proved under exchangeability. The guarantee is then weakened deliberately to characterise the basis-risk inequity that arises when exchangeability fails across agro-ecological zones, and a zone-conditional calibration scheme is proposed to restore coverage within strata. The argument is illustrated with a reanalysis of NASA POWER monthly air temperature at 2 m for Lagos, Nigeria (6.52° N, 3.38° E), 2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 26.414 °C, standard deviation 0.943 °C, and a warming trend of 0.1553 °C per decade.
tags: drought-index insurance; conformal prediction; basis risk; smallholder agriculture; sparse telemetry; risk control; climate analytics
title: Calibrated risk-controlling prediction sets for smallholder drought-index insurance triggers under sparse weather-station telemetry: a climate-analytics evaluation of basis-risk-induced payout inequity

summary: Carbon-credit methodologies for mangrove restoration typically assume that credited carbon storage persists for a fixed horizon, yet staggered enrollment and unobserved baseline dynamics make permanence risk difficult to identify from satellite time series alone. The framework combines a potential-outcomes model for staggered adoption with a hidden-Markov representation of unobserved baseline loss, and derives bounds on the bias of the conventional permanence deduction. Analysis of the identification conditions shows that the standard deduction is unbiased only when baseline loss is independent of enrollment timing, an assumption that fails whenever enrollment is targeted at high-threat sites. The derived bounds imply that permanence-risk overstatement is increasing in the correlation between enrollment timing and baseline threat, and that the sign of the bias can be recovered from observable enrollment-date and land-cover-covariate patterns. The contribution is a diagnostic that credit issuers can apply to existing registries without new field data, together with a formal statement of the conditions under which the conventional deduction is defensible.
tags: mangrove restoration; carbon credits; additionality; permanence risk; causal inference; Landsat time series; staggered enrollment; artificial intelligence evaluation
title: Causal inference on mangrove-restoration carbon-credit additionality from Landsat time series under staggered enrollment: an artificial intelligence evaluation of permanence-risk overstatement

summary: The Western Balkans as a region of developing economies is volatile in economic development at the same time political instability which brings into attention how economic governance is being impacted by political developments and instabilities. This study aims to examine the relationship between political risk and economic governance in the Western Balkans during the period 2002–2023 by using econometric models and quantitative measurements. The investigations focus on six Western Balkan economies. Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, utilizing annual country-level panel data from the World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators and World Development Indicators. The paper applies Fixed Effects and Random Effects panel regression models with Government effectiveness used as the dependent variable and representing economic governance, while political stability is used as the main explanatory variable and an inverse proxy for political risk. The control variables include GDP per capita growth, inflation, foreign direct investment, and trade openness. The findings suggest that political stability is positively associated with economic governance, but the relationship is not statistically robust after controlling for country-specific and year-specific effects.

title: Economic Governance Under Political Risk in The Western Balkans: Panel Evidence From 2002–2023

summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.
title: Phase Organisation Electromagnetic Coupling and Gravitational Receiver Records

summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

summary: Code and results for the paper “Learning Interpretable Dispatch Rules for Aircraft Disassembly under Disruption” (H. Saleh, submitted). summary: For a finite connected graph $G$, let $e(G)$ be the exponent of its Jacobian and $\Delta(G)$ its maximum degree. For each integer $b\ge1$, the simple biconnected graphs with $e(G)\le b$ form finitely many isomorphism classes if and only if $b\le7$; exactly eleven occur with $e(G)\le7$. The simple biconnected graphs with $e(G)-\Delta(G)\le3$ are $K_n$ ($n\ge3$), $C_4$, $C_5$ and $K_{2,3}$. At exponent eight, the number of vertices is unbounded among simple planar bipartite biconnected graphs of maximum degree four. For every integer $r\ge1$, there is a simple planar biconnected graph whose Jacobian is isomorphic to $(\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z)^r$, with explicit divisor generators and an orthogonal decomposition of its monodromy pairing. Every simple $3$-connected planar graph satisfies $2|V(G)|-4\le(e(G)-\Delta(G)+1)^2$ and $2|V(G)|-5\le3e(G)^2/5$. Every simple graph with a cellular torus embedding whose full inverse image in the universal cover of the torus is $3$-connected satisfies $|V(G)|\le e(G)^2$. MSC 2020: 05C25, 05C50, 05C10, 05C40, 20K01.
title: Finiteness thresholds and surface bounds for graph Jacobians

summary: Coordinating molecular, cellular, and macroscopic explanations is a core requirement of secondary biology and chemistry, yet classroom assessments still infer a student's developmental level from written answers collected after an inquiry task ends. Digital process telemetry—the timestamped record of a student's clicks, slider sweeps, pauses, and revisions inside a simulation—captures how learners navigate across scales in real time, but raw interaction counts lack a shared unit of measurement with curriculum learning progressions. This study addresses that measurement gap through a two-part validation. First, a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 86 studies (312 effect sizes; 48,920 learners) synthesized cross-scale inquiry interventions and yielded a pooled Hedges' g of 0.642, demonstrating that adaptive next-step scaffolding, paste-guarded response entry, and explicit cross-scale representations each significantly amplify learning gains. Second, using a fixed-parameter reconstruction of that empirical benchmark alongside a simulated bilingual cohort of 1,240 secondary learners and 1,000 Monte Carlo replications, we calibrated six non-intrusive behavioural trace indicators against a 12-item ordered multiple-choice progression bank on a unified Rasch partial credit logit scale. Common-scale linking error was 0.118 logits (10.9% of the critical Level 2–3 transition interval). Trace-based classifications reproduced item-based progression levels with 81.45% accuracy and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient of .768, exhibited strict measurement invariance across language tracks, gender, and prior achievement, and confirmed that genuine self-regulatory behaviours rather than interface guardrails drive diagnostic classification. Behavioural traces can thus provide calibrated, equitable coordinates for real-time formative support in secondary science classrooms.
title: From Clicks to Constructs: Event-Stream Process Mining, TreeSHAP Attribution, and Rasch Partial Credit Calibration of Behavioural Trace Indicators for Cross-Scale Science Reasoning

summary: Supplementary methods, results, data tables and analysis code for the manuscript Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity. The five resources contain supplementary methods, tables and figures, detailed data workbooks, reproducibility code and supporting audit documentation. Original code is licensed under MIT; original documentation and derived content are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party materials retain their source terms; see LICENSES.md and source notices inside Online_Resource_3.zip. Manuscript abstract Public intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) datasets cover different tissue compartments and measure different subsets of genes, complicating comparisons across studies. We compared four specified gene sets (inflammation, complement, microglial activation and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated oxidative stress) in public paired human brain, single-cell and hematoma-effluent/blood datasets, using patients rather than cells as inferential units. In two studies of paired brain tissue, inflammation, complement and NRF2-associated scores were higher in perihematomal than contralateral samples in all four patient blocks and five matched pairs. Patient-level single-cell comparisons found higher inflammatory and complement scores in microglia/monocyte groups than in comparator lineages. In 14 patients with same-hour paired CD14+ and neutrophil data, a five-gene score named for microglial activation showed a positive CD14+–neutrophil local-response interaction in all 14 (adjusted P=0.000488), but four-program heterogeneity was not established (Friedman P=0.0796). Restricting this score to three shared genes reversed its CD14+ local response; a jointly scaled three-gene interaction was near zero. Independent acute blood data showed positive case-control differences, whereas longitudinal changes were not significant after adjustment. Inflammatory and NRF2-associated expression differences recurred across these datasets. The CD14+ local response of the microglial-related score depended on its measured genes. Version 2026-10-24 changes This revision aligns the five supplementary resources with the current manuscript and adds the exact GSE163256 primary fractional-count-to-score reconstruction and fresh-score downstream verification. Earlier domain-score displays in Online Resource 2, worksheets 05 and 06, are replaced by the fixed-program paired-brain results already used in the manuscript. Superseded, undocumented competitive-null fields are removed from the current Puy13 summary display and export; the defined manufacturer-panel-matched analysis is retained. Scoring and provenance descriptions, archive entry points, fonts, table formatting and numerical display precision have also been corrected. The primary biological scores and current inferential statistics are unchanged. Earlier inputs and execution records are retained with their historical roles identified.
title: Reproducibility materials for Inflammatory and NRF2-associated transcriptional responses in human intracerebral hemorrhage: paired myeloid evidence and gene-set sensitivity

summary: This Zenodo record accompanies the paper “Scalable Measurement-Based Quantum Simulation Patterns for Benchmarking” arXiv.2605.12502   and provides QPatLib v1.0 measurement-pattern datasets in human-readable JSONL together with a ZIP archive of OpenQASM 3.0 circuits used for validation and reproducibility.  The patterns and circuits implement Pauli string unitaries  for benchmark cases.  Cases include all possible string combinations for less than 6 qubits and strings used in Hamiltonians for certain diatomic molecules for 6 or more qubits.     Format:  Each  pattern_*.jsonl file is containins measurement patterns for all subsets for a given model/instance and subset strategy: it begins with a preamble containing model metadata, subset definitions, provenance, and (when feasible) full-pattern test results, followed by one pattern entry per subset. Each subset entry includes a required  pattern_ascii field storing the measurement pattern in the measurement-calculus/Graphix standard with signal shifting, written left-to-right in the canonical order nodes → edges → measurements (with signal dependencies) → byproduct corrections (X/Z). The circuits are included as circuit_files.zip.   Patterns in this record were validated against the corresponding circuits and checked for causal flow.   Codes for generating these patterns can be found at QPatLib repository on Github
title: QPatLib v1.0 — Measurement-based quantum simulation Pauli string unitary pattern collections

summary: Minimal unbiased compositional change generates a source operation algebra with compact internal and Lorentzian event realizations. On the least-dimensional compact connected faithful irreducible orthogonal carrier, independent composition and square-root scaling with unit covariance fix the centred Gaussian law. Its ladder and coherent comparisons generate the round SU(2) S U ( 2 ) process spectrum; complete centre-invariant observations give RP3 R P 3 . Within complete continuations preserving adjoints, exchange structures, source phase and reversal, three theorems characterize relative frames, least faithful matter and the elementary scalar connector. The faithfully acting group is (SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1))/Z6 ( S U ( 3 ) × S U ( 2 ) × U ( 1 )) / Z 6 acting on a sixteen-dimensional full matter module with a fifteen-dimensional charged quotient. The elementary connector has one complex scalar doublet coordinate. The colour connection supplies a collective intensity, Casimir feedback and the long-root drive. The complete spectral response has a unique positive equilibrium at the source-calibrated IR radius Lsrc=2π>Lc=π L src = 2 π > L c = π . Its normalized radial curvature and common-frame coexact response form the generated Yang-Mills mass operator. Its equilibrium Gaussian response completion has a unique vacuum and an attained positive gap. The original connection polynomials embed with their source state and ordinary products intact, and the representation intertwines the equilibrium update. Explicit Hermite weights describe their curvature correlations, and the joint curvature susceptibility detects the collective radial response. A source phase clock calibrates timelike translation on the event carrier. Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction gives free local fields. At gauge-compatible finite internal resolution, causal perturbation theory realizes the native vertices as a local net. Its physical net is the quantum BRST cohomology, with anomaly cancellation ensuring the Ward identities at every order in the renormalizable gauge-matter realization. In the quadratic realization, colour intensity has a radial pole and explicit multiparticle continua.
title: The spectrum of a compact internal space I: Gauge structure and fermion content

summary: Overview This repository contains the replication data, source code, execution logs, and complete analytical outputs for the study: “Detectability of controlled leaks in an Andean water transmission main: a field evaluation of changepoint methods on flow and pressure signals.” The study evaluates the detectability of short-duration controlled leaks using five changepoint and anomaly-detection approaches applied to 30-second flow and pressure measurements collected during two field campaigns in an operational water transmission main in Loja, Ecuador. The evaluated methods are: Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Bayesian Information Criterion (PELT-BIC), Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Akaike Information Criterion (PELT-AIC), Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (BOCD), Cumulative Sum control charts (CUSUM), Moving-average ±3σ control-chart baseline. The repository contains the complete workflow used to: verify field records and ground-truth leak timings; perform campaign-specific spectral analyses using multitaper estimation; evaluate changepoint-detection performance; quantify event-level leak detectability; compare observed performance against chance-level expectations; assess BOCD sensitivity to hazard-rate and threshold settings; generate precision-recall curves and average-precision statistics; perform cross-campaign validation analyses; estimate theoretical detection-delay bounds for flow-based detection. This version supersedes earlier releases by correcting changepoint-index alignment, revising false-alarm-rate calculations using exposure time outside detection windows, replacing pooled spectral analyses with campaign-specific multitaper analyses, and incorporating event-level detectability, chance-level benchmarking, precision-recall evaluation, cross-campaign validation, and theoretical detection-delay analyses. summary: After more than a decade of development, high-resolution spectroscopy plays a central role in the atmospheric characterization of exoplanets, offering insights into planetary chemical composition, thermal structure, and atmospheric dynamics. Among the most intriguing targets for atmospheric characterization are Ultra-Hot Jupiters (UHJs), which, due to their extreme temperatures and intense stellar irradiation, serve as unique laboratories for studying planetary atmospheres under extreme conditions. In this talk, I will discuss what we can learn and what challenges we must confront when interpreting high-resolution observations of UHJs, using KELT-9b (equilibrium temperature ~4000 K) as a benchmark case. Based on transmission and emission observations obtained with the near-infrared spectrograph GIANO-B at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo (TNG), I explore how different modeling assumptions impact the detectability and interpretation of atmospheric signals. In particular, the extreme irradiation conditions of these planets may give rise to departures from local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), making non-LTE effects potentially non-negligible. At the same time, the strong day–night temperature contrasts and asymmetric terminator regions expected in UHJs challenge the applicability of 1D atmospheric models, which may lead to biased or incomplete interpretations of the observed signals.   These effects can have important consequences for the inferred atmospheric abundances and bias the interpretation of key quantities such as the C/O and R/H ratios, which are used to constrain planetary formation and evolutionary scenarios. Addressing these challenges is therefore crucial to robustly link high-resolution observations of UHJs to their origins.
title: INTERPRETING EXTREME ATMOSPHERES: Lessons from High-Resolution spectroscopy of an Ultra-Hot Jupiter

summary: The spectroscopic analysis of cool dwarfs (T_eff < 4700 K) is challenging due to their low effective temperatures, which produce complex spectra dominated by dense molecular absorption bands. These challenges have limited the availability of accurate and homogeneous chemical abundance measurements for these stars. To address these difficulties, we developed AutoSpecFit (ASF) , an automated, line-by-line synthetic spectral fitting code, together with AutoSpecNorm (ASN) , a complementary code designed to perform local pseudo-continuum normalization of observed and synthetic spectra. The combined ASF+ASN framework enables detailed chemical abundance analysis of cool dwarfs using high-resolution optical and near-infrared spectra. ASF employs multiple χ² minimization procedures and iterative optimization to account for the complex correlations among elemental abundances. ASN independently normalizes each synthetic spectrum, ensuring consistent comparisons with observations and reducing uncertainties associated with continuum placement in molecularly crowded spectral regions. Version 2.0 extends the original abundance-fitting framework by introducing an iterative procedure that alternates between the determination of stellar atmospheric parameters and elemental abundances. This approach accounts for the interdependencies between atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances, while employing selected diagnostic spectral lines and iterative optimization to mitigate parameter degeneracies and achieve a self-consistent solution. The updated methodology has been applied to benchmark M dwarfs with independently determined stellar properties, providing an opportunity to evaluate the reliability and consistency of the derived atmospheric parameters and elemental abundances. The ASF+ASN framework has been developed to measure the abundances of up to 15 key elements in cool dwarfs, including major planet-building elements such as C, O, Mg, Si, and Fe. These measurements provide essential constraints on the chemical compositions of exoplanetary systems and their formation and evolution. Furthermore, the application of this framework to metal-poor cool dwarfs offers opportunities to investigate the chemical enrichment history, structure, and evolution of the Milky Way.
title: Detailed Abundance Measurements of Cool Dwarfs: Prospects for Exploring the Galaxy from Stellar Populations to Star-Planet Chemical Connections

summary: One record for each of 18 major U.S. immigration cases of the current period, verified October 23-24, 2026 against primary or near-primary sources (Supreme Court dockets and slip opinions, CourtListener/RECAP dockets and order PDFs - including docket entries read through the CourtListener API - court opinions, and named litigation trackers). Each record gives the caption, court, docket number, category, filing date, the action challenged, a claims summary, a status from a fixed eight-value vocabulary, the latest significant order with source, a docket link, key primary documents, a per-record verification date, and a status-tension field recording disagreements between sources. Version 1.1 adds, per case: the next dated event with its source (plus a forward calendar export; only fully dated events are calendared), structured practical-effect fields (population affected, geographic scope, relief currently in effect with its basis) transcribed from the complaint or operative order named in each record, and an append-only status-change log seeded with the v1.0 baseline. It also resolves the Massachusetts v. Oz summary-judgment hearing date from the docket itself (held October 22, 2026; CourtListener docket 73546826, entry 143). Coverage: birthright citizenship (4), TPS terminations (3), third-country removals (2), asylum access (2), enforcement practices (2), Alien Enemies Act cases (2), Medicaid work requirements (1), parole (1), detention (1). Tool: https://litigation-map.straitresearch.org/. Direction and final calls by Athena Anthea; research judgment and technical execution shared with an AI assistant.

summary: This record contains the replication data and R code for the study “How much does the publication universe matter? Source discontinuities and panel selection in OpenAlex” by Vladislav Bína and Jiří Přibil. The package includes OpenAlex source-by-year counts for 2010–2025 retrieved on 10–11 October 2026, supplementary OpenAlex and Crossref aggregate counts retrieved on 23 October 2026, a provenance-limited earlier archive of annual totals, and twelve annotated illustrative record checks. It also provides eight R scripts, expected numerical results, numerical inputs to the figures, and English documentation. The default workflow reproduces the saved-data analyses offline using base R. It covers publication growth, continuity panels, source turnover, panel-selection timing, population layers, and sensitivity to comparison horizons and endpoints. Version 2.2 was tested with R 4.5.2 on Windows. Data provenance, variable definitions, limitations and reproduction instructions are documented in README.md. Licensing applies by component: bibliographic metadata and factual numerical data/results are provided under CC0 1.0; R code under the MIT License; and original documentation and author annotations under CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE.txt for the exact scopes.

summary: HBB2OBB converts horizontal (axis-aligned) bounding boxes (HBBs) into oriented (rotated) bounding boxes (OBBs) by using existing HBB annotations as prompts for segmentation models from the SAM (Segment Anything Model) family. It targets object detection tasks where objects appear at arbitrary orientations, such as aerial imagery, satellite data, and traffic monitoring, producing oriented boxes that tightly encapsulate non-upright objects without any re-annotation. Beyond conversion, it provides horizontal box detection, evaluation, hyperparameter optimization, an interactive annotation viewer, and annotation format-conversion tools, exposed through both a command-line interface and a Python API. 📖 Documentation: rfonod.github.io/hbb2obb , with a quick start on the bundled sample data, a guide per command, pages on how the conversion works, the confidence score, the metrics and provenance, and a CLI and API reference generated from the code. Why HBB2OBB 🎯 Accurate OBBs from HBBs : prompts SAM-family segmentation models with existing horizontal boxes to fit tight oriented boxes around non-upright objects, with no re-annotation required. 🚗 No HBBs? Detect them : the hbb2obb-detect command runs an Ultralytics detector over the images and writes the horizontal boxes the conversion consumes, confidence column included. 🧩 Model ensemble : combines masks from multiple SAM variants through majority voting for more robust, accurate results. 🛡️ Spatially constrained and safe : region-specific masking and contour refinement keep segmentation inside the object, a mask split by an occluder is fitted back together, and a fallback retains the original HBB when no valid mask is found, counted and reported rather than left to be discovered afterwards. 🔎 Confidence-scored output : every OBB receives a heuristic quality score in [0, 1] that flags silent fallbacks and low-confidence conversions, so you know which boxes to trust; the scores go in the label files or in a side-car directory that keeps them strictly standard, and the detector's own confidence can be carried through instead of, or on top of, that score. 📐 Flexible scaling : positive or negative scale factors, optionally different for the short and long sides, recover cropped object parts or tighten overly conservative annotations. 📊 Evaluate and optimize : evaluation against ground truth on IoU, orientation error, and the share of boxes above a high IoU bar, plus the hbb2obb-optimize command, a hyperparameter search over SAM inference resolution, scale factors, and morphological opening kernel, driven by a configuration file so that a whole benchmark of model ensembles is a single reproducible command. 🔬 Where the score comes from : the hbb2obb-analyze command breaks one evaluation down by the ground truth's orientation, size, frame edge, difficulty and class, and scores the conversion against emitting the horizontal prompt unchanged. 🔄 Five annotation formats : read and write YOLO, DOTA, Pascal VOC, COCO, and LabelMe, for horizontal and oriented boxes alike, with a check that proves every format encodes the same boxes. 🔍 Interactive viewer : the hbb2obb-view command pans and zooms over the annotations, in any format, coloring boxes by confidence and overlaying predictions against ground truth. Where a set ships the same boxes several ways, it names the format on screen and switches between them on a keypress. Features HBB to OBB conversion of YOLO-format annotations using SAM-based segmentation, written in absolute pixels or, with --normalize , relative to [0, 1], the convention Ultralytics reads. HBB detection : produce the horizontal boxes in the first place with any Ultralytics detector, a local file, a link, the Ultralytics catalogue, or Hugging Face, passing any other predictor argument straight through. Multiple model support : SAM, SAM2, SAM2.1, SAM3, Mobile SAM, and FastSAM families. Model ensemble via majority voting for enhanced accuracy. Confidence scoring : a per-OBB quali
title: HBB2OBB: Horizontal to Oriented Bounding Box Conversion and Evaluation Tool

summary: BIODEGRADABLE NANOROBOT MANUFACTURING AND LIFECYCLE ENGINEERING AT THE LIMIT Biodegradable Materials x Functional Manufacturing x Degradation Kinetics This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for manufacturing biodegradable biomedical nano- and microrobots whose functional lifetime and terminal fate can be jointly qualified. Its central problem is a dual-clock constraint: the device must preserve propulsion, structure and interface function throughout a declared mission, then degrade or be retrieved within a separate terminal window without leaving unidentified or high-risk residues. Formula plates state variables, units, assumptions, identifiability, specific blind falsification tests and chapter interfaces. Research Gates specify complete-denominator protocols, analytical evidence, competing explanations, hard stops and successor forks.

summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state

summary: The dataset uploaded here allows replication of the methodology of the study titled "Development and Application of a New Bounded Inequity Indicator for Water Distribution Systems." summary: Replication package accompanying manuscript version 11 of “Pesos endógenos e monotonicidade na mensuração da pobreza multidimensional”. DEA-MP/H measures relative multidimensional deprivation at household level using a fixed DEA reference, nested categorical comparison groups, resource share floors and iterative screening of reference households. The archive contains the R implementation, a single entry point (run_all.R), variable documentation, aggregate empirical results for the Brazilian Demographic Censuses of 2010 and 2022, robustness analyses, computational checks, execution log and SHA-256 manifests. Census microdata and individual intermediate bases are excluded; the scripts obtain official public inputs from IBGE. Empirical applications illustrate the proposed method. Version 1.1.0 corresponds to manuscript v11 (24 October 2026). Code and documentation: MIT license. Repository: https://github.com/moisesluna2026/dea-mp-h
title: DEA-MP/H: replication package for household multidimensional poverty measurement

summary: PRECISION NANOROBOTIC DRUG CARRIER MANUFACTURING AND QUALITY CONTROL AT THE LIMIT Drug Carriers x Precision Manufacturing x Quality Metrology This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for joint batch assurance of precision nanorobotic drug carriers. Its central rule is that attractive marginal averages do not constitute a qualified lot. Particle-size tails, manufactured and biofluid-transformed surface identity, true payload localization, release kinetics, residues and analytical visibility must be measured on representative units from the same unselected batch and adjudicated with their covariance intact. The volume treats the manufacturing process and the measurement system as two coupled sources of risk. Microfluidic mixing time, nucleation, residence-time distribution, fouling, raw-material variation and tenfold scale-up are challenged alongside detector saturation, weighting conversion, dilution artifacts, separation recovery and convenience sampling. A process is not accepted when the analytical chain cannot see the defect it is expected to exclude. The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every Gate begins with a large deep-navy bold question and continues with a blind protocol, evidence package, competing explanation, hard stop and successor fork. The central evidence object is the Carrier Quality Provenance Matrix. It binds raw-material identity, mixer geometry, delivered flows, collection time, sampling inclusion probabilities, raw analytical signals, size and interface distributions, payload mass closure, release curves, storage history and release vetoes. It preserves failed runs and abstentions rather than allowing successful aliquots to redefine the lot.

Version 2.1.0-review includes the original structural and recorded CLI studies, the prospectively frozen 120-question LongMemEval-derived study (two Claude API models, two repetitions, seven policies; 3,360 policy executions), and a separate exploratory 20-question sensitivity study (batch order, revoked-source position, three policies; 1,920 executions). Full public benchmark inputs, frozen protocols, original code, exact recorded requests and responses, usage and spending ledgers, durable SQLite traces, analyses and retention diagnostics are included. Offline reproduction uses recorded responses, disables networking for the reproduction process and requires no API credentials or model charges. Validation included 40 unit tests, the original CLI checks, 3,360 main-study and 1,920 follow-up policy replays, and reconstruction of 128 main-study plus 20 follow-up retrievals. The recorded checks found zero replay discrepancies and made zero new model calls. See verification/ for reports and platform limits. Download and extract recovery-budgets-reproducibility-final.zip, then follow README.txt. The archive contains 26,234 files; online ZIP preview may be unavailable. Correctly weighted live-and-pending quotas and reservations intentionally agree. Episodic memory remains competitive. The separate 20-question follow-up is exploratory and must not be pooled with the 120-question cohort. Scores use strict short-reference EM/F1 rather than official LongMemEval scoring. Replay is computational reproduction, not independent new model sampling. Adaptive-attack robustness, general superiority and production-scale recovery are not established. Anonymous creator attribution is used for review; third-party attribution is retained. MIT applies to original software, CC BY 4.0 to original results and documentation, and LongMemEval retains its MIT notice. Provider services and model weights are not relicensed. The unchanged archive records its preparation-time publication status; this Zenodo landing page and the accompanying release note identify the published release.

summary: INTELLIGENT NANO-ACUPUNCTURE AND CLOSED-LOOP NEUROMODULATION AT THE LIMIT White Rainbow Epoch / 33 × STARLI Original Civilizational Interpretation A Research Flagship in the STARLI White Rainbow Scientific Library ENGLISH DESCRIPTION This prospective research monograph investigates a sharply bounded engineering question: can nanosensing-inspired instrument interfaces and closed-loop neural feedback produce a measurable improvement in feedback latency and electromyographic outcomes when confronted with blinded false-feedback inputs, sensor disconnection, equal-resource conventional controls and independently verified hard-stop conditions? The scientific emphasis is not a one-off demonstration or a claim of proven therapeutic efficacy. It is a technically accountable methodology in which the raw waveform, hardware timebase, stimulus exposure, causal comparator, calibration record, uncertainty budget and right to abstain remain separately inspectable. The work is organized around three couplings: nanosensing, neural feedback and bounded safety. Its larger civilizational frame is Chinese cultural inheritance × modern scientific exploration × original White Rainbow Epoch interpretation. Classical acupuncture and traditional Chinese medicine, Laozi's Daoist philosophy, yin–yang, Five-Phase thinking and the historical vocabulary of meridians or qi are welcomed as cultural and interpretive sources of research questions. They are not relabeled as verified quantum forces, established meridian conductors, or validated clinical mechanisms. The authors' new extensions are explicitly designated White Rainbow Epoch hypotheses, which may be refined, rejected or reformulated through independent experiments. Across 775 pages, the volume contains a scientific-position and provenance dossier; 30 substantive mathematical plates covering distinct routes through optimal control, physical dosimetry, contact mechanics, electromyographic inference, uncertainty propagation, causal identification, robust stability, metrology, quantum-sensor benchmarking, reliability and evidence release; 82 separately introduced chapters with 410 individually paginated scientific studies; 200 expanded Research Gates designed as falsifiable, independently executable research entrances; and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos that propose distinguishable instruments, null-test designs, conditional answers and paths for scientific metamorphosis after a failed hypothesis.

summary: This conceptual theory-building paper develops an interdisciplinary framework for understanding cancer as a model-admissible, potentially persistent system state emerging within complex adaptive biological systems. Building upon evolutionary oncology, dynamical systems theory, cancer-attractor research, tumor plasticity, and adaptive therapy, the study examines how malignant cellular populations may achieve conditional persistence through feedback, selection, environmental constraints, and adaptive reorganization. The central proposition distinguishes biological possibility, dynamical stability, and clinical desirability. Cancer is not described as beneficial or universally stable, but as a pathological configuration whose emergence and persistence may be investigated through formal systems models. The paper integrates three author-developed research architectures: the Akarkach Seven-Stage Emergence Model (A7SEM), A7SEM Reverse, and Pre-Inference Governance Architecture (PIGA). A7SEM provides seven interacting analytical dimensions for studying emergent configurations across biological systems. A7SEM Reverse examines counterhypotheses, contradictory evidence, dependency structures, and falsifiability. PIGA separates the admission of scientific inferences from authorization for consequential actions. Four testable research hypotheses, competing explanations, mathematical templates, and falsification criteria are presented. The framework is further connected to artificial intelligence through structural comparisons involving emergence, uncertainty, observability, and system governance. The study extends the theoretical foundations of the monograph Cancer as a Legitimate System State and connects related publications within the Faith Poetry Research Series. Its principal contribution is an integrated evolutionary, systems-theoretical, and epistemic framework for investigating malignant persistence without conflating mathematical coherence with empirical confirmation or clinical validity. This publication presents theoretical research and a proposed empirical research agenda. It does not establish a validated clinical prediction model, diagnostic procedure, or cancer treatment.
tags: Cancer as a Legitimate System State
title: Cancer as a Legitimate System State: Attractor Dynamics, Evolutionary Plasticity, and Epistemic Governance in Oncology

summary: Here I show my solution to the Hodge Conjecture using my framework and ansatz formulation. The paper starts in 1D, from a simple sieve in mod 9 to a continuum projection, then from a 2D variety in mod 9k, to a continuum projection in 2D which can be map to any elliptic curve with Hasse-Weil operator, doing it back and forward with the inverse operator, linking elliptic curves with continuum topologies or fluid fields, and discovering that the Hasse-Weil function can be the filter we need to detect anomalies, this can allow us to extend this framework to higher dimensions with the master ansatz in 3D.
title: Discrete-Continuum Topology and the Hodge Conjecture: A Compressible Maxwell-Navier-Stokes and Modulo-9 Sieve Framework

summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. Increasing the thickness of transverse rod-like struts in bone-inspired structures was reported to enhance fatigue life by approximately 10–100 times with relatively minor effects on density and stiffness. 🟢 Porosity–strength trade-off: Increasing porosity promotes permeability, vascularization, cell migration, and tissue ingrowth but simultaneously reduces scaffold stiffness, strength, and load-bearing capacity. Therefore, successful scaffold design requires balancing biological benefits against fatigue and mechanical integrity. 🟢 Stress concentration: Geometrical discontinuities and sharp pore corners create localized stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue damage. title: Fatigue behavior of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds: A review

summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. Increasing the thickness of transverse rod-like struts in bone-inspired structures was reported to enhance fatigue life by approximately 10–100 times with relatively minor effects on density and stiffness. 🟢 Porosity–strength trade-off: Increasing porosity promotes permeability, vascularization, cell migration, and tissue ingrowth but simultaneously reduces scaffold stiffness, strength, and load-bearing capacity. Therefore, successful scaffold design requires balancing biological benefits against fatigue and mechanical integrity. 🟢 Stress concentration: Geometrical discontinuities and sharp pore corners create localized stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue damage. summary: Setting up each iteration of a parallel Loop took about 6 seconds on a job directory where writes to disk are slow (ChemAI's /D3), so a 161-iteration loop spent 16 minutes before starting any calculation. The iteration's copy of the database was written in about 70 separate commits; it is now one, taking 0.1-0.2 seconds. The baseline copy each iteration is compared against when its results are merged is now forced to disk before the iteration is used, so that a crash or reboot cannot leave a damaged baseline that a restarted job would trust.

summary: This repository contains the primary data files, analytical matrices, and reproducible R scripts supporting the investigation into eco-morphological decoupling and trophic generalism among sympatric cichlid species in the Cross River Basin, Nigeria. The dataset includes: Mahalanobis morphological distance matrices and proportional Pianka niche-overlap and dietary dissimilarity matrices for eight cichlid species. Processed species-pair tables detailing dietary overlaps, dissimilarity values, and rank mismatch metrics. The complete exact permutation distribution containing all 40,320 species-label permutations of Pearson's correlation coefficient. Fully documented R scripts used for data validation, matrix-level association testing, and figure generation. These resources provide complete transparency and enable the direct replication of all statistical analyses and permutation tests.

summary: This repository provides the replication package for the manuscript Household Vulnerability Screening under Temporal Drift: Evaluation Design, Calibration and Coverage . It contains the code, documentation, generated figures, generated tables, software requirements, and workflow automation scripts designed to support reproduction of the reported analyses. The package is centred on a Python-based analytical workflow covering data preparation, quality checks, variable construction, operationalisation of the Stress × Savings framework, four-state household vulnerability classification, predictive modelling, probability calibration, validation, robustness analyses, and out-of-time performance assessment. A detailed replication guide documents the computational environment, execution sequence, expected inputs, and procedures used to reproduce the reported results. A separate base-R script is provided as an independent cross-check of selected statistical outputs. The underlying survey microdata are not redistributed in this repository. Researchers must obtain the data separately from the World Bank Microdata Library's  Listening to the Citizens of Uzbekistan Survey 2018–2025 (study identifier UZB_2018-2025_L2CU_v03_M), subject to the provider's access conditions. The study is available at: https://microdata.worldbank.org/catalog/6412.
title: Replication Package for "Household Vulnerability Screening Under Temporal Drift"

summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): trends.polyhelper.ai/markets , trends.polyhelper.ai/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

summary: Full FHOPS 1.0.1 rolling-horizon re-run outputs, with the M7 cold-MIP re-run replacing the MIP arm. What changed since v1.1.0-rerun M7 cold-MIP re-run ( 9f0ab69 ): the 117 MIP runs were re-run with the simulated-annealing phase idle (1,800 s stage 1, 900 s earliness, one Gurobi thread per window, 36 windows in parallel), together with the size-40 7,200 s baseline sensitivity runs and the resumed SA run for ni_40_sub112_lock1 . The re-run did not confirm the contention hypothesis. Matching 603,700 per-solve Gurobi records, its work rate was 8.4% higher (median 0.523 → 0.567 work units/s), yet it produced more failures: no-solution windows 9 → 32, empty windows 18 → 39. 20 of 117 runs changed; the long lock1 trajectories diverge, the short ones are identical. The counts describe a time-limited solve, not a fixed property of each instance. Contents data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi/ — SA arm (117 runs) and the original MIP arm. data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi_alone/ — the M7 cold-MIP re-run (117 runs). data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi_sensitivity_* — 7,200 s baseline sensitivity runs. Per-run JSON summaries, stitched assignment tables, solver logs, summary.csv , and the runner / probe / calibration scripts. The paper built from this deposit is UBC-FRESH/fhops-cjfr-rolling-horizon ; its analysis script replays every stitched plan against the full scenario.
title: UBC-FRESH/jaffray-masc-fhops-model: FHOPS 1.0.1 rolling-horizon re-run outputs — M7 cold-MIP re-run

summary: Spatial Methods Workbench is a citation-aware R Shiny environment with 12 guided workflows for spatial autocorrelation, conditional networks, spatially adjusted 2D and 3D networks, spatially varying networks, prediction, clustering, image-regression screening, mediation, and statistical shape analysis. Version 0.4.0 re-targets the three advanced network paths to the current public engines. The ISPat 2D and ISPat 3D paths call the CRAN package ISPAT3D 0.3.1 ( ispat3d_fit_2d for the section-wise planar fit and ispat3d_fit for the pooled volumetric fit: Matern-3/2 Vecchia Gaussian-process adjustment on spatially balanced anchors followed by a shared-plus-zone factor covariance fitted by Gaussian maximum likelihood, reported as signed zone partial correlations). The GP-GHS path calls GPGHS 1.0.1 ( gpghs_graph ) with the shrinkage-factor selection rule and AND symmetry of the accompanying article, and returns the GPGHS edge table with scores and signs. The retired ISPAT 0.1.0, ISPAT3D 0.1.1, and GPGHS 0.1.0 interfaces targeted by v0.3.1 no longer exist upstream. New controls expose factor rank, anchor budget, Vecchia neighbors, optimizer iterations, section handling, threads, and seeds; readiness checks require at least two zones with more rows than markers; result manifests record the engine package, version, and function; and real adapter smoke tests run whenever the engines are installed. This complete source distribution contains the installable Workbench package, Shiny application, five executable vignettes, compact simulated datasets, complete documentation, automated checks, and locally bundled package sources for the exact CRAN ISPAT3D 0.3.1 and GPGHS 1.0.1 engines. install-complete.R installs those local engine copies and the single compiled dependency gpboost without cloning their repositories. A curated public-source bundle also preserves license-safe regression, clustering, neural, SV-NN, STCAR, and SBLF source connected to the Workbench adaptations and related-method provenance. Exact engine calls, built-in adaptations, and related screening workflows remain explicitly distinguished. Large curriculum translations, media, Git history, and platform-specific compiled objects are omitted because they do not execute a Workbench analysis. Installation Download and extract the release, then run Rscript install-complete.R , Rscript verify-installation.R , and Rscript tests/testthat.R . The README contains platform prerequisites, engine options, verification, local launch, Docker, privacy, and troubleshooting guidance. Missing CRAN dependencies may be downloaded; the two direct method repositories do not need to be downloaded separately. Required attribution Users must cite this software release and the method-specific publications or software applicable to the workflow used. The complete bibliography is included in REFERENCES.md and in result bundles. Public sources are identified by repository, commit, version, license, retained scope, and role in vendor/manifest.json . The content is solely the responsibility of the author and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health. Only public, release-scoped material is included in this record.

summary: TripLibre is an open-source, local-first iOS application designed for personal mobility tracking and travel behavior research. It records location data in the background, reconstructs daily travel activities into visits, trips, transportation modes, and trip chains. It allows users to review and correct inferred travel records. The application supports exporting structured mobility datasets in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and SQLite formats, with a Python loader for further analysis. By combining automated GPS-based travel detection with user-controlled data management, TripLibre aims to lower the technical and financial barriers to collecting travel behavior data. Its broader vision is to provide researchers, educational institutions, and resource-constrained communities with an accessible and adaptable alternative to proprietary travel survey technologies, while preserving individual control over sensitive location information. Documentation: https://hhtdiary.org/triplibre/docs/
title: TripLibre: An Open-Source, Privacy-First Travel Diary for Mobility Research

summary: RASHER begins as a fork of BACoN 0.4.0 (commit 4fdec16, which includes the samtools consensus -C 20 change below), adapted to Illumina short reads. Everything under "BACoN changelog" is the parent tool's history, kept for provenance. Changed Renamed throughout: the package, command, log ( rasher.log ) and lock file ( .rasher.lock ) are rasher . The pipeline reads Illumina short reads , paired or single-end. sample_R1 / sample_R2 , sample_1 / _2 sample.R1 / .R2 and sample.1 / .2 files (bcl2fastq _001 tails included) pair into one sample, in flat folders, subfolders and sample sheets; a file without a mate is a single-end sample, and unmated files next to a sample's pairs are skipped with a warning. A pair is baited whole when either mate matches the reference, mates travel together through every step ( 1_extracted/<sample>_R1/_R2 , 2_filtered/... ), and a desynchronised pair is an error, whether the mates carry identical names or /1 /2 suffixes. Baiting aligns with minimap2 -x sr (BBDuk baits pairs natively with in2= / outm2= ). --keep-bam now keeps the baited reads aligned to the reference (paired samples: a proper paired BAM). Filtering: fastp (adapter trimming, quality and length filters; its JSON and HTML reports land in logs/2_filter/ where MultiQC finds them) followed by deterministic, evenly spread subsampling of the reads (pairs kept whole) to --target-depth . Filtlong, --keep-percent and --filter-by-reference are gone; --min-read-length defaults to 50. Fasta reads skip fastp and are filtered by length. Templated assembly aligns pairs with minimap2 -ax sr and calls samtools consensus -X hiseq (call quality at least 20, as BACoN's unreleased change at the time of the fork). De novo assembly: SKESA ( -a skesa ; the recommended de novo assembler — on the real-data benchmark its SNP distances matched SPAdes' with far fewer contigs) or SPAdes ( -a spades , --isolate ; writes the assembly graph, more robust below ~30x depth). Flye and myloasm are gone, with --read-type and --min-size . --snp-method auto is minimap2 for templated assemblies and SKA2 for SPAdes and SKESA assemblies. -m/--memory also sizes SPAdes and SKESA (it was BBDuk-only). A paired sample X next to a sample named X_R1 or X_R2 is an error (their outputs would collide). No assembler flags circular contigs any more, so SKA2's circular-contig end extension no longer applies. Single-end extraction matches read names with a trailing /1 or /2 stripped, as aligners report them. Output folders of BACoN do not resume under RASHER (the checkpoint fingerprints are seeded with the tool's name; every step runs again); BACoN VCFs are rewritten. Checkpoints record each step's own output signature, and a result is only reused when its output is still the file it wrote: a sample returning to a sheet can no longer pick up reads another sample wrote over. Switching a sample between single-end and paired (or fasta and fastq) removes the other shape's files. BBDuk's paired outputs are checked mate against mate, like minimap2's (a desynchronised pair fails the sample); mates named .1 / .2 ( fastq-dump --readids ) pair; the unpaired-reads file of fasterq-dump --split-3 next to its pair is skipped with a warning; a file cannot pair with a link to itself, and files that look like mates but do not pair are warned about. Stale fastp reports are removed on rerun and for samples that fail at baiting. The report and MultiQC drop the circular-contigs column (no short-read assembler flags circles) and say that read pairs were kept whole when either mate matched.
title: RASHER: Bait, Assemble and Compare Illumina short reads

summary: Entity Matching identifies records that refer to the same real-world entity across one or more data sources. It is a key step in data integration and data cleaning. In practice, real-world datasets are often incomplete, and missing attribute values can significantly reduce the accuracy of traditional and learning-based methods. This presentation introduces a technique that uses Sentence Transformers to address EM under incomplete data. Records are represented as dense semantic embeddings, which allows the approach to capture contextual similarity between tuples even when some attribute values are missing. These embeddings support both the recovery of missing information and the matching of records. Experiments on benchmark datasets with varying levels of missingness show that the approach improves the robustness of entity matching on incomplete data.
title: A Sentence Transformer Based Technique for Entity Matching within Incomplete Data
